articles.title: Aneel confirma bandeira verde na conta de luz em novembro
articles.summary:
A conta de luz dos brasileiros continuará sem cobrança adicional em novembro. A Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) anunciou, nesta sexta-feira (30), que manterá a bandeira tarifária verde pelo segundo mês consecutivo. A decisão significa que os consumidores não terão taxas extras relacionadas ao sistema de bandeiras tarifárias na fatura de energia elétrica.
Segundo a agência, a manutenção da bandeira verde ocorre por causa das condições favoráveis de geração de energia, impulsionadas pelo aumento das chuvas nas regiões onde estão concentradas as principais usinas hidrelétricas.
Com os reservatórios em situação mais equilibrada, não há necessidade de acionar em maior escala as usinas termelétricas, que produzem energia a custos mais elevados.
De maio a setembro, a bandeira tarifária permaneceu amarela, o que representava cobrança adicional de R$ 1,88 a cada 100 kWh consumidos. Em outubro, a Aneel já havia reduzido a classificação para verde.

articles.title: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
articles.summary:
While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents built by aliens.
Some scientists have suggested that extraterrestrial civilizations, if they exist, could be billions of years older than humanity. Such civilizations might have developed technologies far beyond humanity’s, including forms of AI.
Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence. At the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California, agents can now steer the instrument, enhance and correct incoming data, and apply AI models to the incoming stream — all from a single natural language request. The NVIDIA Holoscan platform processes the massive streams of sensor data, giving agents live data to act on.
The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies.

articles.title: Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
articles.summary:
Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
Today, Cloudflare services for private origins is generally available. Point a proxied DNS record at a private IP, and Cloudflare reaches the origin over your existing Cloudflare One connection. Your origin stays private, while web application firewall (WAF), caching, bot management, and Workers work just as they do for public origins.
In June, we launched this capability in closed beta to address a problem we kept hearing from customers: Their internal APIs, AI agent backends, MCP servers, and operational tools weren’t built to face the Internet, but those services still need to accept requests from partners, customers, or agents over the Internet. Before the beta, putting Cloudflare in front of these services meant exposing a public IP, opening a firewall port, or running cloudflared alongside the origin.
Those requirements often left private applications without the same protections and controls they used for public applications, including WAF, bot management, rate limiting, caching, traffic acceleration, rewrites, and Workers.
What is generally available today
During the closed beta, eligible customers requested access through their account team. Today, we’re opening access beyond that beta group.
Point a proxied A or AAAA record at a private IP, and Cloudflare’s application services work as they do for public origins:
- WAF and managed rules

articles.title: Ruidos extraños y pérdidas de agua: señales de que tu lavadora necesita mantenimiento
articles.summary:
La lavadora soporta cientos de ciclos de lavado al año, pero ese uso constante termina por desgastar sus componentes internos. Reconocer a tiempo las señales de desgaste permite evitar averías mayores, reparaciones costosas y la necesidad de reemplazar el equipo antes de tiempo, además de garantizar que la ropa salga limpia.
La mayoría de las fallas en este electrodoméstico no ocurren de forma repentina: casi siempre existen alertas previas que anticipan un problema. Ignorarlas puede derivar en daños por agua o en averías que comprometen la seguridad del hogar. Saber identificar estos síntomas ayuda a prolongar la vida útil del aparato.
La acumulación de humedad genera malos olores
Los olores a moho o humedad dentro de la lavadora suelen originarse por residuos acumulados en la junta de la puerta, el dispensador de detergente o el tambor. Ventilar el equipo después de cada uso y limpiar la junta con un paño seco reduce la proliferación de hongos y bacterias. Realizar ciclos de limpieza con agua caliente una vez al mes también contribuye a eliminar olores persistentes.

Cuando las prendas salen con manchas, olor desagradable o sin la limpieza esperada, el problema puede estar en el agitador, el impulsor o en residuos acumulados en el tambor. articles.title: $6 Billion Binance Hack Bears Hallmarks of North Korea’s TraderTraitor
articles.summary:
Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has been hit by the biggest crypto heist ever recorded, and blockchain intelligence firms say North Korean state-sponsored hackers are the likely culprits.
Binance has put the damage at roughly $6.3 billion. TRM Labs, which followed each transfer on-chain, calculated about $6.36 billion siphoned from Binance wallets across ten blockchains on October 29. Most of the money left within roughly 20 minutes.
The haul dwarfs the $1.5 billion taken from Bybit in February 2025, which previously held the record. Binance has halted withdrawals and pledged to reimburse all losses using company funds and its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU).
The exchange’s early findings suggest the intrusion may have started with an employee’s laptop.
“Binance’s initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak,” Binance stated.
TRM’s analysis shows the attackers spent at least a day and a half getting ready. The wallet used to run the operation was funded with a few small Tornado Cash withdrawals, and the malicious code was trialed on other wallets before going live.
On Ethereum, the attackers leveraged EIP-7702, a mechanism through which a standard wallet can delegate its behavior to a smart contract by signing a permissi…

articles.title: Ataque à Binance: Trump comenta suspeita de envolvimento de hackers norte-coreanos
articles.summary:
O governo dos Estados Unidos está investigando se hackers ligados à Coreia do Norte foram responsáveis por um ataque que desviou cerca de US$ 6,3 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 34 bilhões) da Binance, maior corretora de criptomoedas do mundo. A possibilidade foi comentada pelo presidente Donald Trump nesta sexta-feira (30), enquanto empresas especializadas em análise de blockchain apontam indícios de envolvimento de um grupo hacker norte-coreano.
Questionado por jornalistas no Salão Oval da Casa Branca sobre a possível participação da Coreia do Norte, Trump respondeu que o governo estava investigando o caso. “Estamos analisando isso”, afirmou. O presidente também reconheceu que houve um ataque hacker, mas não confirmou a autoria.
A suspeita ganhou força após análises da TRM Labs e da Chainalysis, duas empresas especializadas em rastreamento de transações com criptomoedas. As companhias identificaram semelhanças entre o incidente e operações anteriores atribuídas a hackers norte-coreanos.
A TRM Labs apontou o grupo TraderTraitor, unidade de hackers de elite ligada à Coreia do Norte. A empresa afirmou ter alto grau de confiança nessa atribuição, conclusão que também foi compartilhada pela Chainalysis. A Binance, porém, ainda não confirmou quem realizou o ataque.

Aktie stürzt ab: Warum Intel unter dem KI-Boom leidet, von dem es eigentlich profitieren wollte
Der Chipriese Intel hat auf einen Schlag mehr als ein Fünftel seines Werts verloren, weil die Geschäftsprognose des Konzerns die Börse schwer enttäuschte. Intel macht zu schaffen, dass wegen des explosiven Anstiegs der Speicherpreise weniger PCs verkauft werden. Schwaches PC-Geschäft belastet Intel

articles.title: 4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys
articles.summary:
4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys
On October 19, 2026, we learned about eMudhra’s eight shockingly weak keys: where eMudhra was trusted to pick a 115-digit number for their virtual combination lock protecting the Internet, they picked the number 4. Not even four digits, just the number 4. The other seven keys were similarly weak: 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237.
The next day, we wrote a blog post on the immediate action we took to mitigate this leak, and what customers needed to do on their end to stay secure. Now, we are sharing a more in-depth follow up on the evidence we’ve seen of exploitation, and the progress seen on visitors patching their systems.
Let's start with the scale of the problem. A certificate authority (CA) with weak keys this serious is unprecedented, and the potential consequences are significant. While there have been plenty of compromised certification authorities in the past (such as DigiNotar, TÜRKTRUST, and TrustWave), access to their keys has always been contained to a degree; these incidents gave a limited set of attackers or organizations the ability to issue fraudulent certificates. The eMudhra incident is fundamentally different; the affected intermediate private keys could be recovered almost instantly by anyone from the public certificates themselves. articles.title: TeamViewer Flaw Could Let Malicious Hosts Take Over Support Technicians’ Machines
articles.summary:
A high-severity vulnerability in the popular remote-access tool TeamViewer could be exploited to take over a viewer’s (an IT support technician’s) system, cybersecurity firm Remedio warns.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111585 (CVSS score of 8.8), the flaw is described as an integer overflow affecting the remote-control screen processing component of TeamViewer clients across Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.
Successful exploitation of the security defect could allow attackers to crash the viewer’s TeamViewer or execute arbitrary code on their system.
“Exploitation requires a user to establish a remote-control session to an attacker-controlled or compromised host,” TeamViewer notes in its advisory.
The issue, Remedio says, is rooted in how the host’s screen dimension is transmitted and used in the viewer: the host announces the geometry of the screen and the viewer uses the received dimensions to allocate an in-memory pixel buffer it then uses to decompress incoming screen updates.
This decode surface is only used if a hardware video decoder is not available for the session, but the host may refuse to negotiate the video codecs, thus forcing the viewer to that path.
A host can request a surface larger than what a screen can reach, and the path accepts it. An example would be 32768 by 32768 pixels at 32 bits per pixel, which overflows 32 bits, with every row past 31 being written out of bounds.

Tracked as CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS score of 10/10), the flaw stems from insufficient regular expression validation in Onigmo, Ruby’s regular expression engine.
The bug “could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration,” GitLab noted in an October 12 advisory.
According to Alpine Linux, a threat actor targeted its GitLab instance with a CVE-2026-97229 exploit on October 20 and 21. The attack failed, but the Linux distribution rebuilt the instance from scratch.
“Our checks show that the aports repository, packages, and the October 21 releases were not tampered with,” Alpine Linux notes.
It is still testing the GitLab instance before public release, and has reset all passwords, warning of observed automated login attempts using passwords compromised in other leaks.
As part of the October 20-21 attack, the hackers used a newly registered account to send crafted CI configurations to Alpine Linux’s GitLab instance, crashing the worker process.
“In 4 of those crashes, the attacker got partway through the exploit and failed at the next step. The attacker also downloaded our GitLab container image, which suggests they were tuning the exploit to our exact build. We have found no evidence that the attacker ran code on the server, but we cannot r…

articles.title: Por qué MrBeast afirmó que tiene su cuenta bancaria “en números rojos” a pesar de su fortuna
articles.summary:
Jimmy Donaldson, conocido como MrBeast, tiene 28 años, más de 600 millones de seguidores y una empresa valorada en cerca de 5.000 millones de dólares, según Fortune. Pese a esas cifras, el youtuber afirmó en una entrevista con el The Wall Street Journal que su cuenta bancaria está en negativo
“Tengo dinero en negativo ahora mismo. Pido prestado. Todos los que ven este vídeo tienen más dinero que yo en su cuenta bancaria”, aseguró.
El patrimonio de MrBeast no es efectivo disponible
Según Celebrity Net Worth, la fortuna de Donaldson rondaría los 2.600 millones de dólares en 2026, pero casi la totalidad de ese monto proviene de su participación en Beast Industries, el holding empresarial que controla. El youtuber posee algo más de la mitad de una compañía que vale 5.000 millones sobre el papel, aunque esa valoración corresponde a acciones, no a dinero líquido.
El mismo mecanismo explica por qué figuras como Elon Musk o Jeff Bezos encabezan los listados de las personas más ricas del mundo: su patrimonio incluye participaciones en empresas como Tesla, SpaceX o Amazon que, si se vendieran de golpe, provocarían una caída en el precio de esas acciones. Por esa razón, estos empresarios no necesitan vender sus participaciones para costear sus gastos personales.
Pedir prestado resulta más barato que vender acciones

Pour revenir à la raison, la marque lui adjoint un petit frère, le Segway Xyber Air, présenté le 14 octobre et disponible depuis ce mardi 27 octobre aux États-Unis : il entre cette fois dans les classes légales de vélos électriques américaines, et coûte bien moins cher.
Fini la moto à pédales, bonjour le vélo fatbike électrique

L’architecture est désormais semi-rigide et non plus tout-suspendue, le cadre affine ses tubes, la suspension avant est moins importante (80 mm vs 110 mm), tandis que la batterie migre sous le tube supérieur.
Segway conserve les grandes lignes comme la longue selle, mais on est en présence d’un véritable nouveau modèle, à la manière du MacBook Air face au MacBook Pro. Les roues 20 pouces à bâtons – et non plus à rayons – possèdent également des pneus inédits, de largeur 4 pouces (vs 5 pouces), avec un seul petit garde-boue arrière. Le freinage reste hydraulique, mais l’étrier avant 4 pistons du Xyber laisse place à un 2 pistons.

articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.summary:
Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. Prefieren fiestas-evento en entornos con cierto carácter y selección de público (por lo menos un par de palabras con alguien).
¿De dónde viene? En parte de la pandemia.
Los que ahora tienen veinte años fueron confinados justo en la edad de fiestas hasta el amanecer. Los primeros amores. En algunas ciudades se organizaron fiestas clandestinas (fuera de club) en viviendas particulares. Cuando se levantaron las restricciones, no regresaron a la pista habitual. Surgieron colectivos que organizan música (también de artes visuales) y vida social en pisos o lugares recuperados. Cada vez con más personalidad.
En Italia (de donde partimos) pueden ir a ver a un artista emergente colombiano en un club. También pueden ir a una cascina (casa de campo) que queda a media hora de coche de la ciudad y bailar. Existen colectivos que organizan eventos al aire libre. Maratones de música (de día y de noche) en entornos naturales (también en teatro o museo). Incluso se ha hecho cool ir a determinados lugares. Le processeur ne fait pas tout. Pour vendre un ordinateur, il faut aussi pouvoir l’équiper en mémoire à un prix acceptable. C’est précisément là que le marché se grippe : les composants deviennent plus chers, les machines aussi, et les acheteurs se montrent moins pressés de renouveler leur équipement. Cette situation frappe directement Intel. Après la publication de ses résultats, jeudi 29 octobre, son action a plongé de plus de 20 % dans les échanges suivant la clôture de la Bourse américaine. Les investisseurs s’inquiètent surtout des prochains mois, alors que le fabricant prévoit un ralentissement durable du marché du PC.

Face à des ventes moins dynamiques, les constructeurs cherchent à écouler les ordinateurs qu’ils ont déjà en stock et réduisent leurs commandes. Pour Intel, la conséquence est immédiate : moins de machines à assembler signifie aussi moins de processeurs à vendre. Le groupe anticipe un recul du marché du PC d’environ 12 % en 2026, puis de 10 % supplémentaires en 2027.

Drupal is urging online store owners to patch a highly critical access bypass vulnerability in the Commerce Core module, warning that it is being exploited in the wild.
Tracked as CVE-2026-118539, the issue affects a contributed module that adds e-commerce features to Drupal websites, including a shopping cart and checkout process. Drupal’s statistics show the module is used on more than 42,000 sites.
“The module doesn’t sufficiently protect certain routes and entity fields, leading to an access bypass that may financially impact the vendor,” Drupal explains in its advisory.
The Drupal security team gave the issue a risk score of 21 out of 25. According to the score, unauthenticated attackers can exploit the flaw no matter how the module is set up.
Drupal has confirmed the attacks but has not said how the bug is being exploited, who is behind the activity, or how many sites have been targeted. It has also not said whether the vulnerability was exploited as a zero-day, before patches became available.
The vulnerability affects 3.x versions before 3.3.13 and earlier releases before 8.x-2.41. Administrators should update to one of the two fixed versions and review their store orders.
“Sites should audit their orders for inconsistencies as this vulnerability is being actively exploited,” the advisory reads.

Most hybrid cars you can buy today are parallel hybrids, which means that they have an internal combustion engine and an electric motor, both of which drive some or all of the wheels—everything works in parallel. But there’s another approach. Instead of connecting the engine to the wheels via a transmission, it can act as a generator and charge the traction battery, which in turn powers the electric motor. Since the engine and motor work in series, this is known as a series hybrid.
That’s mostly how the Chevrolet Volt worked. As does Honda’s hybrid CR-V. The best advice once your company achieves product-market fit? Don’t get stuck on things that got you there, keep adjusting your architecture and workflow to fit your new realities and sizes.
Starting strong is one thing, but the real point is pushing past the growth ceiling without crashing: McKinsey found 78% of products launched successfully only to fail later on. Having worked in international expansion, I have seen how the practices that help a startup gain traction can cause troubles as it grows. Here is my top-5 of what’s better to be changed once a company is too big for a startup mode, and what habits are worth keeping in mind.
Money moves faster than decisions
Congratulations, it’s been your big funding round. Having more capital can feel like you have almost unlimited freedom to chase everything at once. This money mostly goes to ideas that already work, more on tests, all at once. In a ten-person startup, the founder knows every ongoing experiment. In a 100-person company, nobody does. Tests overlap, compete for the same target audience, and rarely get switched off. Meanwhile, decision-making slows down as more people have something to say. More money won’t fix messy operations, it just makes the mistakes more expensive.

articles.title: Windows 11 : plus besoin d’Adobe Acrobat, Microsoft Edge va devenir le meilleur lecteur de PDF
articles.summary:
Il existe plusieurs façons d’ouvrir des documents PDF dans Windows 11. La première, en passant par un outil dédié, comme SumatraPDF, Foxit Reader ou encore Adobe Reader.
Il est également possible de faire appel à des services en ligne, mais la manœuvre est généralement déconseillée, d’autant plus s’il s’agit de PDF contenant des données sensibles.
Enfin, la dernière option existante pour ouvrir vos PDF est d’utiliser tout simplement votre navigateur Web. Qu’il s’agisse de Chrome, Edge ou encore de Firefox, tous les navigateurs Web actuels sont capables d’ouvrir ces fichiers. Certains proposent même quelques outils d’édition basiques qui permettent de remplir, signer ou encore d’annoter vos documents.
Mais jusqu’à présent, pour la gestion même de ces documents et des pages qui les composent, seules les applications dédiées étaient dotées du nécessaire. Google’s satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth
The Project Suncatcher satellite generated a haiku about being in space.
Blue marble below
Data streams in silent grace
Starlight feeds my core. ✨
Google says it tried out other space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts as well. The test is part of Google’s Project Suncatcher, an experimental initiative that could eventually put AI data centers in space. Google launched the satellite into orbit earlier this month.

articles.title: North Korean hackers blamed for stealing record $6.3B in Binance breach | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Hackers working for the North Korean regime have been blamed for a record cryptocurrency heist following a cyberattack at crypto exchange Binance. The hackers stole at least $6.3 billion in crypto from the company’s wallets, though about half of that amount was frozen as the stolen crypto traveled across various blockchains, according to security researchers.
The breach is by far the largest known theft of crypto in history, though the incident has not been confirmed yet to be resolved, and the amount of crypto stolen may change.
In a post on X, Binance said its initial investigation showed that the hackers broke into the company’s network after targeting a “compromised” Binance engineer’s laptop, which “allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.”
Binance said it has seen no evidence of a leak of its private keys, which would grant the hacker near-unfettered control over the company’s stores of crypto.
The crypto exchange — the world’s largest — said it has now suspended all deposits and withdrawals while its investigation into the breach continues. TechCrunch reported on Thursday that the exchange had paused withdrawals across some of its blockchains.
Binance said “user funds are safe,” but did not immediately provide proof of this claim. The company said it will “publish an updated proof of reserves once the remediation is complete.”

articles.title: Fresh WordPress Vulnerability in Attackers’ Crosshairs
articles.summary:
Threat actors started exploiting a new high-severity WordPress vulnerability within hours of patches rolling out, Defiant warns.
Patched on October 28 in WordPress 7.1.4, the security defect impacts the WordPress update process and can be exploited for remote code execution.
According to Defiant, it is a race condition in WordPress’s Core update process that can be exploited without authentication. The attack complexity, however, is high. No CVE identifier has been assigned to the vulnerability yet.
The weakness stems from predictable, web-accessible staging paths during the upgrades. New files are unpacked into a predictable directory that is accessible from the web on many servers.
“The attacker needs a full-package update containing the installer files, public web and PHP access to the staging tree, a predictable or discovered staging path, and enough time to complete the attack before WordPress cleans up the temporary files,” Defiant explains.
According to the web security firm, threat actors are already attempting to exploit the vulnerability, polling the vulnerable paths repeatedly in their attempts to hit the seconds-long exploitability window.
While an attacker does not need an account on the site to exploit the flaw, they do need “to hit a very narrow window while WordPress is unpacking a complete Core update,” Defiant says.

articles.title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in record crypto heist
articles.summary:
Binance has suspended all withdrawals after the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange fell victim to what appears to be the biggest heist in history.
The exchange put the “estimated total impact” of the hack at about $6.3 billion and said around $3 billion of affected assets, mainly stablecoins that act as cash for the crypto market, had been frozen.
But analysts at Elliptic said the attacker had changed about $3.3 billion into digital assets that could not be frozen and was working to cash those out as traditional currency.
An “initial investigation” suggested hackers had been able to compromise an engineer’s laptop and withdraw funds from the platform, Binance said, adding on Friday morning that further investigation “has uncovered additional points of breach.” The company is working with law enforcement.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs linked the hack with a North Korean unit known as TraderTraitor, saying that the sums involved would make it “the largest crypto theft on record.” Last year, North Korean hackers stole crypto worth $1.5 billion in an attack on exchange Bybit.
Peter Ward, of the Sejong Institute in Seoul, said North Korea had considerable expertise and offered “near-total protection to its hackers.”
“Things may get a lot worse going forward,” he said.

Udezue said reducing the cost of inference, the process through which AI models generate responses and perform tasks, was essential to making the technology affordable for businesses and individuals across the continent.
“Our goal is to make AI cheaper for Africa and America,” he said. “The future of AI really goes through inference.”
His argument shifts attention from the race to build more powerful models to the economics of putting them to work. For businesses using AI to answer customer enquiries or support employees, the expense recurs each time the system performs a task. Those costs can determine whether a promising application becomes viable for everyday use.
Udezue highlighted the gap between the cost of using AI and what many Africans earn, warning that access to a tool means little if people cannot afford to use it consistently.
The distinction matters as companies seek to integrate AI into their operations. A service affordable for occasional queries may prove too expensive when used throughout the working day or offered to thousands of customers. Lower inference costs could make those applications more commercially practical.

Now, scientists are using artificial intelligence to investigate their experiences, uncovering unexpected symptom reports that differ from those documented in clinical trials.

articles.title: Alerte WordPress : 22 failles corrigées, les pirates ont riposté en 9 minutes chrono
articles.summary:
Des hackers cherchent à s’engouffrer dans une brèche qui peut exposer un site WordPress pendant sa mise à jour. La version 7.1.4 corrige le problème depuis le 28 octobre, mais Wordfence a déjà repéré plus de 18 500 requêtes suspectes.
Il n’a fallu que quelques heures pour que des attaquants tentent de profiter de l’une des failles corrigées par WordPress 7.1.4. Le 28 octobre dernier, Wordfence, le spécialiste de la sécurité des sites WordPress, a ainsi repéré une première requête suspecte neuf minutes seulement après l’activation de sa règle de protection, elle-même déployée environ trois heures après la publication de la mise à jour.
Le piège se cache dans les fichiers temporaires
La faille, signalée par le chercheur Umut Bayram, concerne le cœur de WordPress, des versions 4.7 à 7.1.3. Lors de certaines mises à jour utilisant un paquet complet du logiciel, les fichiers sont décompressés dans un dossier temporaire au nom prévisible, sous wp-content/upgrade. Cette copie contient un installateur auquel un visiteur peut accéder si le serveur laisse ce répertoire accessible et autorise l’exécution de PHP. Dans ces conditions, un attaquant sans compte peut parvenir à exécuter du code sur le serveur.
Les hackers doivent toutefois accéder à l’installateur temporaire avant que WordPress ne supprime les fichiers. Selon les essais rapportés par Wordfence, ils ne disposent que de quelques secondes. Ils envoient donc des requêtes à répétition dans l’espoir de surprendre un site au moment…

articles.title: Invictus, l'avion hypersonique européen qui vise Mach 5 pour 2032, franchit une étape clé
articles.summary:
En aéronautique, rien ne se perd, tout se transforme. Dans les années 1990, l’entreprise britannique Reaction Engines Limited se met en tête de créer un avion spatial nommé Skylon. Son moteur hybride Sabre devait fonctionner comme un réacteur jusqu’à Mach 5 (cinq fois la vitesse du son), puis comme une fusée pour emmener l’appareil jusqu’en orbite.
Mais au bout de plusieurs décennies de tests, d’études et de partenariats, notamment avec le groupe BAE Systems et l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA), le projet tombe à l’eau : faute d’avoir trouvé de nouveaux investisseurs, Reaction Engines fait faillite fin octobre 2024.
Hypersonique et réutilisable
Pourtant, l’ESA garde dans un coin de sa tête cette idée de moteur hybride, et sa pièce maîtresse (un échangeur qui refroidit en une fraction de seconde l’air brûlant aspiré par le moteur) est reprise pour un autre projet : Invictus. Cet avion hypersonique expérimental doit pouvoir voler à cinq fois la vitesse du son, décoller et se poser sur une piste classique. Le programme a franchi une étape clé, comme l’a annoncé le 23 octobre Stephan Carroll, ingénieur en chef d’Invictus chez Frazer-Nash, le cabinet d’ingénierie britannique qui pilote le projet, dans une publication sur LinkedIn.

Teams building AI applications need a repeatable path from a model configuration to a working inference endpoint. NVIDIA Dynamo is a distributed inference framework that coordinates model serving across GPU workers. Deploying it on Kubernetes is only a first step. A successful model deployment requires more: GPU drivers, resource allocation, scheduling, networking, and monitoring must all work together. Resolving these dependencies takes time away from testing model behavior, serving performance, and application integration.
The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform brings together technologies to help the ecosystem design, build, and operate more efficient AI factories, and Dynamo is one of them. To make management of those infrastructure dependencies easier, the platform contains NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR). It packages NVIDIA Dynamo and its supporting infrastructure into validated recipes. Each recipe defines a configuration for a specific environment and workload, including pinned component versions, compatibility constraints, and validation checks. AICR gives platform teams a repeatable way to deploy and check the runtime, providing developers with a consistent foundation for serving models and testing applications.
This walkthrough covers the infrastructure that supports Dynamo on Kubernetes, compares two routing options, and shows how to deploy and validate the runtime with AICR.

articles.title: What five P99 CONF talks reveal about database trade-offs
articles.summary:
What five P99 CONF talks reveal about database trade-offs
P99 CONF is a virtual conference on high-performance, low-latency applications. Its 2026 event ran October 21–22. Here, we cover five of its 60-plus sessions. The recordings are available on demand at p99conf.io after registration.
Database storage design balances read amplification, write amplification, and space amplification (RUM conjecture). Improving one can increase another, depending on the workload and configuration. The five talks below show how engineers make those trade-offs across different database systems.
“Can Everything be an LSM?”
Almog Gavra, Co-Founder at Responsive (now Databricks)
Gavra frames database design around read amplification (data read per result), write amplification (data written per logical write), and space amplification (storage used relative to live data). A log favors fast writes but makes reads work harder; a sorted array does the reverse. As Gavra put it, “I think about LSM trees as a mechanism for tuning between these two extremes.”
LSMs were built for local disks, but their immutable files also fit object storage. Gavra points to Amazon S3’s lower storage cost, durability, and availability, then names the trade-offs: objects must be replaced rather than edited, each GET and PUT has a price, and cold reads are slower. In his example, a local NVMe cache miss takes about 150 microseconds, versus 20–30 milliseconds for S3 Standard — roughly two orders of magnitude. LSMs batch write…

articles.title: Algo extremadamente raro está pasando en el ártico: la rotura del vértice polar más temprana desde que tenemos registros
articles.summary:
El lunes 26 de octubre, con los datos de las 12 de la noche, 18 de los 50 escenarios que calcula cada día el Centro Europeo de Predicción a Medio Plazo decían que el vórtice polar iba a romperse en los quince días siguientes. Doce horas después eran 23. El martes, 43. El jueves 29, los 50 decían eso mismo.
No es solo algo de Europa. En los últimos tres o cuatro días, los principales modelos de predicción han ido confluyendo en la misma idea: que el vórtice va a sufrir una inversión (con los vientos de la estratosfera cambiando de sentido) entre el 4 y el 10 de noviembre.
Si ocurre, tendremos entre manos un calentamiento súbito estratosférico, sí; pero no uno cualquiera. El más temprano desde 1958: unas tres semanas antes del que hasta ahora tenía el récord. Esto lo podemos dar casi por hecho. Lo que pase luego, nadie lo sabe.
¿Qué es exactamente el vórtice polar? Se trata de una corriente de fuertes vientos (oeste → este) que gira en torno a las grandes reservas de aire frío que se encuentran sobre los polos del planeta. Se forma en la estratosfera; es decir, a unos 16–48 kilómetros de altura. En sentido metafórico (o 'periodístico' si me apuran), el vórtice polar es lo que encierra el frío en el polo.
La lógica nos dice que, en verano, el vórtice se reduce hasta la mínima expresión y, aunque es cierto que nunca lo hemos visto desaparecer del todo en estas fechas, se hace tan débil que apenas influye en el tiempo del hemisferio.

Dans ses résultats financiers du troisième trimestre publiés ce jeudi 29 octobre, la filiale électrique de Harley-Davidson dit douter de pouvoir poursuivre son activité au cours des douze prochains mois. Cette mention comptable, appelée « going concern » aux États-Unis, signifie que la direction n’est pas sûre de pouvoir financer l’entreprise d’ici un an. Dans la matinée, l’action du constructeur a perdu plus de 40 %, a relevé Electrek.
Pourtant, les ventes progressent : 241 motos électriques entre juillet et septembre 2026, contre 184 un an plus tôt. Sauf que la branche moto a perdu 17 millions de dollars d’exploitation sur la même période, soit environ 70 000 dollars (équivalent à 62 500 €) par moto vendue. Sa trésorerie est tombée de 82,8 millions de dollars fin 2025 à 39,9 millions au 30 septembre, et une dette arrive à échéance en décembre 2027.
Pour mémoire, Harley-Davidson avait sorti sa première moto électrique en 2019, avant de faire de LiveWire une marque à part entière en 2021. Depuis, la gamme s’est étoffée avec les modèles S2 Alpinista, Del Mar Mulholland et dernièrement avec les petites motos S4 Honcho. Aux États-Unis, LiveWire revendique 80 % des parts de marché sur les motos électriques de plus de 50 kW (67 ch) depuis janvier.

articles.title: The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping
articles.summary:
OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that publishers can use to opt out of being scraped by AI, as reported earlier by Search Engine Roundtable. With this control, publishers can apply their AI training preferences across multiple AI companies, instead of setting them individually.
The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping
The new control will allow publishers to apply their AI training preferences across multiple crawlers.
The shared “policy token” signal is proposed by Kevin Kelley, a technical lead for standards at Anthropic, as part of the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF). It will live within a website’s robots.txt file, which has long signaled which web crawlers can and can’t scrape a site — whether for search indexing, archiving, or AI training. Currently, sites have to signal their AI training preferences separately to each AI company.
The announcement comes as publishers grapple with the continuing influx of AI crawlers scraping their sites and feeding their content into AI models. Some companies and organizations have attempted to combat unauthorized scraping, with the Really Simple Licensing (RSL) standard giving publishers the ability to charge crawlers that visit their sites, and Cloudflare blocking AI crawlers by default.
OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will restrict their AI crawlers from accessing a site if they encounter the shared token. Meta communications head Andy Sto…

articles.summary:
Razer is often called the Apple of the gaming laptop industry. Like the MacBook Pro, the Razer Blade series is famed for being slim, stylish, powerful, and overly expensive. But does the Blade 18 with its RTX 5090 live up to that reputation, both the good and the bad, and can it compete with my favorite desktop replacement, the very similar Lenovo Legion 9i Gen 10?
The Blade configuration we received for review is an absolute beast of a gaming machine. In addition to packing Nvidia's flagship 24GB mobile GPU (175W TGP), there's a 24-core Intel Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus, 32GB of DDR5-6400, a 2TB PCIe 4.0 SSD, and a 99Wh battery. There's also a dual-mode 240Hz/440Hz IPS display, which we'll get to later.
Thanks to the memory crunch, gaming laptops are priced like second-hand cars right now, but few are more expensive than this $5,400 machine.
The slim and sleek descriptors are definitely warranted here. It's amazing how Razer fits all this hardware into a chassis measuring just 15.74 × 10.84 × 1.10 inches. It's the same thickness as the Legion, in fairness, but more compact in its other dimensions.
It's also noticeably lighter at just over 7 pounds, making it easier to carry around than many other 18-inch laptops.
The Blade is stylish. The CNC-milled chassis, with its black anodized finish and illuminated green Razer logo, makes this look like the laptop Darth Vader would use. In a good way.

articles.title: Bulletproof Host Virtualine Loses Its Domain to FBI Seizure
articles.summary:
The FBI has seized virtualine.net, the domain of a Russian-speaking bulletproof hosting services provider associated with various cybercriminal operations.
According to court documents, Virtualine, also known as Secury, Massgod, Spamhouse, Lanedo, and Omegatech, has been hosting customers’ illicit services and helped them evade law enforcement takedown attempts.
In posts on cybercrime forums, Virtualine promoted support for various types of cybercriminal activity, including phishing, spam, carding, and more; advertised its ability to move customer services to unaffiliated infrastructure; and claimed it intentionally ignored abuse.
It also allowed users to post and sell explicit images and videos of minors and adults, and supported at least one customer that offered a hack-for-hire service aimed at stealing sexually explicit content from online accounts.
Despite receiving numerous takedown requests from law enforcement agencies in several countries, Virtualine continued to aid the customer and even helped them create a new website for uploading the illicit content. The provider continues to host the new website.
According to blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs, Virtualine has been used, among others, by ransomware groups and an infostealer operator.
“Virtualine received more illicit-attributed cryptocurrency than any other TRM-labeled bulletproof hosting provider, despite receiving less total value than several peers,” the company says.

Tyler Shultz didn’t need to see “You Can See Everything” to make up his mind about Holmes. Shultz, whose first job out of college was at Theranos, was a key whistleblower who exposed the company’s dangerously inaccurate blood testing devices, which made their way into Walgreens stores and delivered faulty results to real patients. articles.title: Why Trust Is Becoming Essential for Agentic Commerce | BetaKit
articles.summary:
When tickets for your favourite artist go on sale in the middle of a critical meeting, the idea of dispatching an AI agent to buy them for you sounds pretty appealing. But how do you know it will buy the right tickets, stick to your budget, and keep your payment information safe?
“Trust is foundational to agentic commerce being able to truly scale.”
Answers to those questions are becoming more important as agentic commerce scales in Canada and AI agents move from recommending purchases to making them. A Mastercard report predicts that by 2030, more than one in 10 online shoppers will routinely use agents to shop and pay.
Making those purchases secure takes a lot of work behind the scenes, and trust built into every side of the transaction. As the buyer, you need to trust the agent to follow your instructions. The seller has to know it’s legitimately acting on your behalf, while the financial institution needs to verify that the purchase matches what you authorized before approving the payment. All of this must happen in real time, with safeguards against fraud and attempts to manipulate the agent.
Canada is already putting the technology to the test. This fall, Mastercard worked with AI company Flybits and credit card issuer Rogers Bank to complete its first Canadian transaction through Agent Pay, its agentic commerce service. articles.title: GM to pay $220 million after selling customer Smart Driver data
articles.summary:
General Motors marketed its Smart Driver system as a way for parents to monitor teen drivers or for adults to track their driving behavior. But in 2024, it emerged that GM had been sharing that data with brokers. Those brokers then sold the data to insurance companies, and some drivers found that their insurance became more expensive as a result. To make matters worse, many of those drivers claimed they had no knowledge of ever agreeing to share such data for such purposes.
Last year, GM and its OnStar subsidiary entered into a settlement with the FTC, prohibiting them from sharing some kinds of driver data with third parties. The settlement was finalized this January. That agreement banned the two companies from sharing geolocation data or driver behavior data for five years. At the time, GM also discontinued Smart Driver across its entire range.
Now the automaker has reached terms with the District of Columbia and 35 states after their attorneys general joined together to sue GM as well.
GM said in a statement that “[s]afer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share.”
According to TechCrunch, the settlement with the states is notable in a third party is required to assess GM’s compliance with the new privacy program.

articles.title: GPT-6.1 Terra vs. GPT-6 Astra: One sacrifices accuracy for lower cost and higher speed at high effort
articles.summary:
GPT-6.1 Terra vs. GPT-6 Astra: One sacrifices accuracy for lower cost and higher speed at high effort
OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on October 26, marketing it as a cheap, fast model for high-volume everyday work, priced at a tenth of its GPT-6 Astra flagship.
As the mid-priced model in its GPT-6 family, OpenAI lists Terra at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, a mere tenth of Astra’s $10 and $50. The AI giant also reports that Terra completes tasks more than three times faster than Astra in its Agents’ Last Exam benchmark. Those computer-use results are not directly comparable to the three tests below.
Early benchmarks showed some limitations, alongside gains. Plotly reported that Terra caught three of five planted patterns in its analytics test and passed 40 of 43 questions overall. Artificial Analysis found that it guessed on 38% of questions it couldn’t answer instead of saying so, down from 88% for GPT-5.6 Terra in the same benchmark. Cost management for generative AI is a shared responsibility between the teams that build applications and the teams accountable for cloud spend. Many teams start by comparing per-model token rates and asking application teams to shorten prompts. Those steps help, but they don’t answer the questions that finance and engineering leaders ask as usage scales: which team spent this, on which workload, and was that spend inside an approved budget?
Agentic workloads make those questions more pressing. A conversational assistant typically issues one model invocation per user turn. An agentic workflow, such as an AI coding assistant that plans a change, reads files, calls tools, and iterates, issues many invocations per task and carries a larger context on each one. Token consumption therefore scales with the degree of autonomy you grant the workflow and the size of the context it carries, rather than with the number of user interactions. Because consumption is a function of how a workload is designed and operated, cost management for generative AI is an architectural and operational discipline. Published averages are a poor substitute for your own numbers: use the AWS Pricing Calculator and the Amazon Bedrock pricing page to model rates, and use Step 2 of this post to measure what your workloads actually consume.

articles.title: Counting agents is the wrong scoreboard: Better questions for enterprise leaders
articles.summary:
Counting agents is the wrong scoreboard: Better questions for enterprise leaders
Not how many agents, but which outcome. Not can it advise, but can it execute.
Ask a room of executives about agentic AI and within about ninety seconds someone will ask how many agents they ought to be running. It has become the default measure of progress: a number you can put on a slide, benchmark against a competitor, and report upwards.
It is also the wrong question.
Senior Vice President for Oracle UK & Ireland.
Across the 200-plus workshops my team and I have run with enterprises in Europe and the Middle East, the organizations getting real value from AI tools are not the ones with the longest agent inventory. They are the ones who never framed the problem that way to begin with. They started by identifying a business problem or point of friction and worked backwards. Everyone else started from the technology and went looking for somewhere to put it.
There are four questions I hear constantly that are quietly steering good companies into Pilot Purgatory. Here they are, and here is what I would ask instead.
Don't ask how many agents. Ask what outcome you are improving.
Much of the last two years of enterprise AI has been about helping people work faster. Copilots that answer questions, assistants that summarize the meeting you have just sat through, tools that get you past the blank page. These are genuinely useful and I would encourage everyone to switch them on.
But speed is not the same …

articles.title: Passkeys Are Better Than Passwords. But They Are Not Enough.
articles.summary:
For decades, passwords have been one of cybersecurity’s most persistent weaknesses. Users forget them, reuse them, share them, and surrender them to convincing phishing sites. Attackers steal credentials, automate credential stuffing, and increasingly use artificial intelligence to make social engineering more effective.
What are passkeys?
Passkeys promise to eliminate much of this problem.
Built on public-key cryptography, passkeys replace shared secrets with cryptographic credentials. There is no password for an attacker to steal, intercept through phishing, or reuse against another service. Properly implemented passkeys are also phishing-resistant because authentication is bound to the legitimate service.
That represents a significant improvement over passwords and many traditional forms of multi-factor authentication (MFA). But it does not answer a more fundamental question: Just because someone successfully authenticated, should we continue to trust that identity?
Passkeys strengthen authentication. They do not eliminate identity risk.
What Passkeys Get Right
Traditional authentication frequently relies on passwords combined with one-time passcodes, SMS messages, or push notifications. While stronger than passwords alone, these methods remain vulnerable to phishing, adversary-in-the-middle attacks, MFA fatigue, SIM swapping, and social engineering.

If demand from the US military is added in—and SpaceX does not extend the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy program to accommodate increased national security needs—the shortage could be doubled.
“What we wanted to get at is to understand how severe this launch crisis is and when will it be resolved,” said Caleb Henry, director of research at Quilty Space. “What we learned is that the launch crisis is more severe than we thought and that it will not go away this decade for sure, and it might not abate until sometime late in the 2030s.”
The report tallies a number of familiar factors that have gone into this crisis: the war in Ukraine taking Russian rockets off the Western market; Amazon Leo demand; developmental delays in a new generation of rockets, from New Glenn and Vulcan to Neutron, Terran R, and Nova; and more recently, the retirement of the Falcon 9 as a rocket for commercial service.

Breet, founded in 2019, converts cryptocurrency into cash for individuals in Nigeria and Ghana. It also offers an application programming interface that allows businesses to accept crypto payments and receive settlement in local currency.
The proposition separates the payment method from the currency a merchant ultimately wants to hold. Customers can pay with digital assets, while businesses receive local money without having to build a crypto operation of their own.
For Mbene, the objective is to reduce the work required to complete that transaction. “We’re just obsessed with simplicity,” she said.
That approach places much of the complexity behind the scenes. Functions such as monitoring transactions, routing deposits and converting currencies need to work together without requiring merchants to manage each step themselves.

- Share:
A swimming robot does not necessarily need a bulky motor or powerful mechanical parts to move through water. MIT researchers have demonstrated that a single, carefully engineered layer of living muscle cells can generate enough force to propel a tiny robot forward.
The engineers developed an extremely thin swimming robot that uses living muscle tissue to move its fins. Described in a new study published in Advanced Functional Materials, the device has a flexible gel framework roughly the length and width of a stick of gum. The gel forms two fins, each coated with a layer of muscle cells far thinner than a human hair. These cells have been genetically modified to contract when exposed to light.
By directing light onto either fin, the researchers can trigger muscle contractions that make the fin flap and push the robot through water. Adjusting which fin receives light and how frequently it is illuminated allows the team to control both its speed and direction.

articles.title: Drupal warns of critical Commerce Core flaw exploited in attacks
articles.summary:
Drupal warned admins to patch a critical access bypass vulnerability in the Commerce Core module that attackers are exploiting in the wild.
Tracked as CVE-2026-118539, this flaw stems from a missing authorization weakness that can be abused by unauthenticated attackers and affects Commerce Core versions 0.0.0 through 2.41 and 3.0.0 through 3.3.13.
The Drupal security team asked admins on the 3.x branch to upgrade immediately to Commerce Core 3.3.13 (or Commerce Core 8.x-2.41 for earlier versions) and audit orders for inconsistencies, since threat actors are exploiting this vulnerability in attacks.
"This module enables you to sell goods and services to customers through an included shopping cart and checkout form or through decoupled applications via APIs," Drupal said in a Wednesday advisory tagged as highly critical.
"The module doesn't sufficiently protect certain routes and entity fields, leading to an access bypass that may financially impact the vendor. This vulnerability is being actively exploited in the wild."
Commerce Core is a community-developed Drupal module used by more than 42,000 websites, including many high-profile organizations such as Fortune 500 companies and research universities.
The module provides a software framework for building and running e-commerce sites and shopping apps on top of the Drupal Content Management System (CMS).

articles.title: Smaller Components Complicate BGA Rework Heating- EE Times
articles.summary:
Smaller components and denser boards are creating new thermal challenges for ball grid array (BGA) rework. Miniature passives can be located within a millimeter or two of rework targets. This tightens thermal profile windows and raises the stakes for precision heat delivery. Traditional hot-air systems that operated at larger scales struggle to meet the demands of today’s high-density assemblies.
The SMT miniaturization trend behind modern PCB design
The drive toward higher functionality in smaller form factors has pushed surface mount technology (SMT) miniaturization to the forefront of PCB design priorities. Designers are packing more components into less space, with passive components such as 0201 and 01005 footprints increasingly used in high-density applications.
The International Electronics Manufacturing Initiative (iNEMI) electronics roadmap identifies component miniaturization and increased packing density as important industry drivers, with HDI microvia sizes continuing to shrink as manufacturers push toward finer geometries. This trend creates new challenges for rework operations that were engineered around larger geometries.
Proximity and warpage risks in high-density assemblies
As spacing tightens, the gap between a target BGA and its neighboring 0201 or 01005 passives can fall below a millimeter. Standard hot-air nozzles weren’t designed for this proximity.

Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.
Emerging evidence suggests some people with eating disorders are misusing weight-loss drugs.
GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are one of the biggest biotech breakthroughs of the last decade. But to some clinical psychologists, they can represent something more sinister—a potential trigger for eating disorders.
A new report suggests that the global incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa shot up between 1990 and 2023—by a whopping 71%. By 2023, there were an estimated 18.1 million people living with one of these two disorders.
What’s worse is that the number is likely to be much higher than that once we factor in other eating disorders. And, disturbingly, those in the field are already starting to see GLP-1 weight-loss drugs exacerbating the issue.
Cheri Levinson is a clinical psychologist at the University of Louisville in Kentucky who has specialized in eating disorders for almost 20 years. She says she’s now seeing more patients with more severe symptoms than at any other time in her career, and that many of them are misusing GLP-1s. “This is the worst I’ve seen things,” she says.
Eating disorders are mental health conditions in which people’s eating behaviors impact their health. They include anorexia nervosa (defined by a fear of weight gain), bulimia nervosa (in which people binge and purge), binge eating disorder, and others.

Le phénomène existe bien, mais ses effets sur la météo en France dans les prochaines semaines restent très incertains, y compris pour les prévisionnistes.

Qu’est-ce que le vortex polaire ?
Comme l’explique Météo-France, le vortex polaire correspond à une « zone de basses pressions en altitude centrée sur les pôles géographiques ». Cette zone est toujours présente près des pôles, indique le National Weather Service, qui précise bien qu’il ne s’agit pas d’un phénomène nouveau. « Le terme ‘vortex polaire’ n’a été popularisé que récemment, attirant ainsi l’attention sur un phénomène météorologique qui a toujours existé », souligne le service météorologique des États-Unis.

The open-source MPC Sample Key won’t be focused on chopping up drum breaks.
While the Sample Key shares many of the same controls as the MPC Sample — including the three context-sensitive encoders, a large main encoder — it seems designed for pitched sample playback, rather than chopping up drums. In fact, the “chop” button from the MPC Sample is missing entirely from the Sample Key.
The dedicated pitch and mod wheels are another clue there. But there are also buttons for changing the octave range of the 25-key keyboard, as well as ones labeled “chord” and “arp.” Presumably, those enable a chord playback mode and an arpeggiator. While using an arpeggiator to play back drum samples can be a fun way to create rhythms, it’s more commonly used for melodic and bass parts. And a chord mode would be basically useless for drums. Those options also appear to replace the chop function from the standard MPC Sample.

articles.title: Josep Albors, experto en ciberseguridad, sobre apagar el móvil como aconseja Sánchez: “Para la mayoría de los usuarios sirve de poco”
articles.summary:

Josep Albors, responsable de Investigación y Concienciación de ESET España, comenta: “Para la mayoría de los usuarios, que nos enfrentamos a amenazas más mundanas, este consejo, en materia de ciberseguridad, sirve de poco”. Además, dependiendo de cómo se instale y active, el programa malicioso tendrá efecto o no.
“Solo se aplica para casos concretos en los que el malware está presente en la memoria RAM, que se borra cuando reinicias el dispositivo”, explica Albors. El problema de esta memoria es que es temporal y se vacía al apagar el teléfono. En el caso de que la infección solo se active en memoria (sin persistencia), puede ser interrumpida por el apagado.
El problema es que, si el software malicioso está instalado en el terminal, al apagar y encender el móvil no va a desinstalar la app maligna. Así pues, puede volver a activarse al encenderlo. Además, no podemos estar seguros de que la infección haya desaparecido por el hecho de que el móvil vuelva a funcionar correctamente. Es necesario conocer la naturaleza de la amenaza y trabajar sobre su causa.

Ghanaian startup TrustCheck has built a review and trust platform that allows consumers to check out businesses, especially social media sellers, before they part with their money.
Launched in January of this year by Elliot Brenya, Tema-based TrustCheck lets users look up a business, read verified customer reviews, and see a trust score out of 100. The score combines a business’s rating, review volume, how responsive it is to customers, verification status and any open disputes.
“A lot of buying in Ghana now happens on Instagram, TikTok, X and WhatsApp. You see a product, message the seller, send money by Mobile Money and hope it arrives,” Brenya told Disrupt Africa. “Most of the time it does, but when it doesn’t, there is usually no way to get your money back and no record that warns the next person. TrustCheck is meant to be that record.”
Brenya was inspired to build the platform after being scammed while buying a mobile device, having relied on fake ratings for the vendor.
All reviews on TrustCheck are moderated before going live, and reviewers can attach proof of purchase, such as MoMo receipts or order chats, which only moderators can see. Businesses cannot pay to have reviews removed, but can claim their pages for free, respond to reviews and apply for verification. Le fonctionnement historique de la plate-forme, qui dure depuis près de vingt ans, va évoluer pour devenir accessible uniquement sur connexion.

Il explique d’une part qu’avec l’immensité du site, la navigation sans algorithme de recommandation sur celui-ci ne fonctionne pas correctement. Il évoque aussi le fait que certaines fonctions clés de Reddit, notamment la possibilité de commenter, rejoindre une communauté ou encore voter, requièrent une connexion à la plate-forme.
Mais ce nouveau système de fonctionnement que Reddit souhaite mettre en place vise surtout à protéger la plate-forme contre le scraping (l’extraction) non autorisé de ses données par les intelligences artificielles. Reddit déplore en effet que les robots d’entraînement des IA collectent sans autorisation les contenus publiés sur ces pages accessibles sans connexion pour entraîner leur modèle. CVE-2026-97229 stems from an integer overflow weakness and could let remote attackers run arbitrary code on targeted instances via a maliciously crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient expression validation.
"GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation," it said.
GitLab addressed the security issue in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE) versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8 and urged admins to patch their servers immediately.

articles.title: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
articles.summary:
Crater counts tell us that most of the Martian surface is more than 3 billion years old, but pieces of Mars we have on Earth tell a different story. The three main classes of Martian meteorites—shergottites, nakhlites, and chassignites—are all 2.4 billion years old or younger. Until now, only two genuinely ancient Martian meteorites were known: Allan Hills 84001, found in Antarctica, and a jumbled rock from northwest Africa nicknamed Black Beauty. Now we have a third one.
A team led by Yang Liu, a planetary scientist at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, has shown that a Martian meteorite called Teghaza 001, found in the Sahara Desert in Mali in 2022, formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. “It’s very old and similar to some of the oldest rocks on Earth,” Liu says.
A filtered collection
“We don’t fully understand why old Martian rocks are so rare on Earth,” Liu said. Part of the answer may lie in how a piece of Mars gets here. It takes a large impact to launch a rock off the planet, and not every rock can survive that. “If the impact hits into loose powder, it may not get cemented to become a rock and fly off Mars’ gravity,” Liu said. “So the natural impact already acts as a filter. Weak rocks do not make it off Mars.”
That left scientists with a biased collection.
“Even to date, none of our collected Martian meteorites are similar to what we found on the surface,” Liu said. The partial exception is Black Beauty, which has a bulk chemistry that matches orbital measurements. But…

articles.title: Netflix Titus Adds Single-Tenant VM Isolation for Containers
articles.summary:
Netflix has added single-tenant Titus, a mode that runs one task alone on its own right-sized EC2 instance. The Compute/Platform team still owns and patches the host, so application teams keep the same API and deployment path. First adopters include stateful, high-throughput streaming workloads. Here, a neighbor's interference can lead to minutes of checkpoint recovery.
Titus launches millions of containers a week across tens of thousands of EC2 instances and is multi-tenant by default. Netflix says that cgroups, seccomp, the iocost controller, and traffic shaping can’t split shared hardware. This includes resources like the last-level cache and memory bandwidth. Its HTB traffic shaper also takes a global lock. A container that floods the host with small packets can burn the kernel CPU and starve its neighbors. Predictive CPU pinning and eBPF-based detection helped, but Netflix concluded that shared-kernel tuning narrows the gap without closing it.
Netflix rejected the alternatives for specific reasons. MicroVMs such as Firecracker and Kata need bare-metal or nested virtualization, and nested virtualization was not ready on Netflix's instance types. They also meant running a hypervisor layer, added virtualization overhead, and lacked GPU support. gVisor added overhead on I/O-heavy paths, and a single vendor does most of its maintenance. articles.title: Binance loses $6.3 billion in largest crypto heist ever
articles.summary:
What we know so far: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, has suffered a cyberattack believed to be the largest crypto theft in history. Crypto worth more than $6 billion has been stolen from the platform, which initially suspended customer deposits and withdrawals. It's believed that a North Korean hacking unit was responsible for the attack.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs puts the haul at approximately $6.36 billion, taken from Binance wallets across ten blockchains on October 29. Most of the money was moved in about 20 minutes. The firm attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking unit, with high confidence.
There is some good news for customers. Binance says it has worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in affected assets and will cover all losses. Deposits are now operating normally, although withdrawals remain suspended. The exchange said on Friday that it expected withdrawals to resume within the next day or two.
The initial investigation pointed to a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer. Binance said this allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawals. It added that it had found no evidence that wallet private keys had leaked.
However, the company subsequently said investigators had uncovered additional points of breach, describing the incident as a complex attack – so the compromised laptop is unlikely to be the whole story. Binance has promised to release more…

articles.title: SS7 and Diameter Attacks: How Signaling Flaws Expose Your Phone
articles.summary:
SS7 and Diameter signaling attacks can track, intercept, and impersonate you. Here’s how they work and how to stop them.
Your phone can be tracked, your SMS two-factor codes can be intercepted, and your number can be impersonated, all without malware, a phishing link, or any access to your device.
The attacks happen inside the telecom network, in the carrier-to-carrier control protocols known as signaling, the automated descendants of the old telephone switchboard. Most users never see them, and most carriers can’t reliably stop them.
Signaling attacks aren’t new. Most recently, they made headlines when Iranian-linked actors reportedly exploited outdated network technology to locate the phones of US personnel in the Middle East during the Iran war.
But the vulnerability has been around for decades, and it’s been used for far more everyday crimes, like intercepting bank one-time passcodes. It has even been demonstrated by popular YouTubers: Veritasium hijacked a tech influencer’s calls and texts using only his phone number.
This keeps happening
- Criminals have reportedly exploited signaling protocols in attacks on bank accounts and global telecom infrastructure.
- Citizen Lab exposed two long-running commercial surveillance campaigns abusing SS7 and Diameter, with thousands of attacks against targets in dozens of countries.

articles.title: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Investors are getting nervous about AI infrastructure spending just as the Big Tech companies double down.
Over the past two weeks, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft have outlined plans to spend more than $740 billion on capital expenditures this year, which Wall Street is reading as AI infrastructure spending, including data centers and chips.
Earlier in the AI boom, investors largely rewarded such big outlays, viewing them as a sign of confidence in the technology’s growth potential. But as we enter the fourth quarter, that enthusiasm seems to be giving way to concerns about negative free cash flow (spending more cash than a company brings in), mounting debt, and whether these enormous investments will ever generate enough returns.

articles.title: Netflix Treats GPU Reliability as a Distributed Systems Problem
articles.summary:
Netflix has detailed how it is building a reliability platform for large-scale GPU training and inference, using layered health checks, automated remediation, and fault-tolerant training to keep jobs running despite hardware failures.
The problem is particularly acute for large AI training jobs. A model may run for weeks across hundreds of GPUs, with all workers operating in lockstep. A single failed GPU, degraded network adapter, or slow machine can therefore stop or significantly slow the entire workload. Netflix has built its GPU compute platform on Kubernetes and designed it to detect these failures, remove unhealthy capacity automatically, and allow long-running jobs to recover from machine loss.
The approach has produced measurable results: Netflix reports more than 99.95% GPU-node availability and an increase in job success from approximately 98% to more than 99.5%.
A conventional cloud health check can establish that a virtual machine is running and reachable, but that does not mean its GPUs are capable of running a distributed training workload.
Netflix found that a GPU can respond normally to a status query while failing once memory is allocated or sustained computation begins. Similarly, a network adapter may be present but have fewer links than expected, allowing collective operations to continue at severely reduced bandwidth.

Este escenario podría cambiar gracias a la Z2RAM, una nueva tecnología impulsada por el antiguo jefe de Intel, Pat Gelsinger.
De acuerdo con un reporte de The Register, la propuesta de la Z2RAM intenta combinar las ventajas de las tres tecnologías que dominan el mercado: SRAM, DRAM y NAND.
La SRAM es extremadamente rápida y se utiliza en las memorias caché de los procesadores, pero ocupa mucho espacio y es costosa de escalar. Mientras tanto, la DRAM ofrece una mayor densidad y es la base de la memoria RAM convencional, aunque es más lenta. Por último, la NAND, que se usa en los SSD, se distingue por su capacidad y fabricación en múltiples capas verticales.
Nagare Labs, una startup respaldada por Geslinger, intenta reunir lo mejor de estos tres mundos. Según la compañía, Z2RAM podría ofrecer la velocidad de la SRAM, la densidad de la DRAM y la arquitectura de la NAND en un mismo paquete. Esta nueva memoria sería escalable y tendría un consumo energético mucho menor, convirtiéndose en una alternativa para las empresas de IA.

articles.title: Over 25% of people lie to get antibiotics—and their lies aren't even good
articles.summary:
A significant number of patients in the US lie to their doctors to get antibiotics they likely don’t need, according to two new studies. While that may not be a startling revelation, the studies drills down on the phenomenon, finding that the lies patients tell are generally bad ones—and yet, they work almost all the time.
In the two linked studies published Friday in JAMA Network Open, a team of researchers led by Alistair Thorpe at the University of Utah analyzed online survey data from over 1,000 adults. They found that over a quarter of people reported having lied to a clinician at least once to get an antibiotic prescription for themselves or a child in their care. Patients lied by either exaggerating symptoms, making up symptoms, or—most often—both.
But interestingly, the lies people told to get antibiotics involved making up or exaggerating symptoms of infections that wouldn’t be treated with antibiotics. For example, the most common falsehoods were symptoms associated with colds, such as fever, cough, and sore throat. That’s despite the fact that colds are caused by viruses, not bacteria—which antibiotics treat.
Further, while the data suggests many patients were being dishonest, clinicians responded with what could be considered their own form of dishonesty; in most cases, the dubious fibs led to antibiotic prescriptions. articles.title: En 1965, París empezó a excavar un aparcamiento frente a Notre-Dame. Se encontró con una ciudad romana entera bajo sus pies
articles.summary:
Hace más de 60 años, la ciudad de París ideó un plan para excavar un aparcamiento junto a su catedral más famosa. La excavación se alargó más de lo previsto, ya que sacó a la luz unos dos mil años de historia de la ciudad, apilados capa sobre capa. De hecho los restos siguen ahí, bajo el pavimento, y millones de visitantes cruzan la plaza frente a Notre-Dame cada año sin saber qué hay debajo.
Lo que hay es la Cripta Arqueológica de la Île de la Cité, un museo construido en torno a los restos que afloraron cuando París se preparaba para construir el aparcamiento a principios de la década de los 60.
Qué pasó. La excavación comenzó en 1965, justo antes de la construcción del aparcamiento subterráneo bajo la plaza, según el Ministerio de Cultura francés. Y duró hasta principios de los 70.
En los trabajos se encontraron una barbaridad de estructuras y elementos que datan de la época romana. El propio ministerio enumera un sistema de muelles galorromanos, casas con hipocaustos (calefacción bajo el suelo) y una sección de muralla de la época romana tardía.
París Musées cuenta además que se encontraron baños públicos y por encima de esas capas se encuentran niveles medievales con pozos, sótanos de casas y hasta los cimientos del Hospice des Enfants-Trouvés del siglo XVIII (la institución central donde acogían a recién nacidos y niños abandonados en la Francia del Antiguo Régimen). articles.title: Waiting for an AI law is a poor compliance strategy
articles.summary:
Waiting for an AI law is a poor compliance strategy
India's courts and sectoral regulators have already begun assigning liability for AI failures. Businesses that are holding out for a statute are preparing for the wrong deadline.
A bank has an AI system in place to flag suspicious transactions and take the call to freeze accounts. While the workflow has a human sign-off in place, clearing around 400 cases a day has resulted in the approval system becoming a formality. So, when a wrongly-frozen account takes the system to court, the bank becomes unable to prove what the human actually reviewed. This, unfortunately, is no longer a hypothetical scenario.
On July 2, 2026, the Supreme Court of India quashed orders passed by the National Company Law Tribunal and the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal in the Pooja Ramesh Singh v. Jammu and Kashmir Bank Ltd. case. The orders had rested on citations generated by an AI tool and attributed to the Supreme Court itself. This directed the Bar Council of India to constitute a committee to prescribe disciplinary norms for advocates who file AI-generated citations.
This is a business story as much as a legal one. Despite two tribunals and several rounds of proceedings, the parties had to carry the cost of a machine error that no human caught before filing. No AI statute was required to reach that outcome. Ordinary law, applied by judges, did the work.

articles.title: Doomformer: Diese KI wurde in Doom geschaffen – was sie leisten kann
articles.summary:
Doomformer: Diese KI wurde in Doom geschaffen – was sie leisten kann
Egal, ob in der Google-Suche oder auf einem Satelliten der ESA: Doom wurde mittlerweile auf so vielen verschiedenen Plattformen spielbar gemacht, dass die meisten Gamer:innen wohl schon lange mit dem Zählen aufgehört haben. Etwas seltener sind die Versuche, etwas anderes als einen Ego-Shooter aus Doom zu machen. So versucht es derzeit der Entwickler, der sich auf GitHub den Nicknamen „mottopanikeiku“ gegeben hat.
Doom als KI? Wie das funktionieren soll
Sein Projekt trägt den Namen „Doomformer“ und ist eine Wortneuschöpfung aus Doom und einem Transformermodell. Im Grunde hat er den Ego-Shooter in ein neuronales Netzwerk umgewandelt, das in der Lage ist, Arithmetik durchzuführen. Um das zu realisieren, nutzt er sogenannte „Voodoo Dolls“ aus Doom. Das sind Klone der Spielfigur, die immer dann auftauchen, wenn das Spiel einen zusätzlichen Spielerstartpunkt im Level entdeckt.
Um das neuronale Netzwerk zu bauen, werden laut dem Entwickler 1.355 Voodoo-Puppen genutzt, die zusammen ein MNIST-Netzwerk auf der Map bilden. Die Puppen fahren auf Bahnen hin und her und überqueren dabei Linien, die als Gewichtungen fungieren. Kommt es zu einer Aktivierung der Puppen, wird eine bestimmte Anzahl über eine Treppe nach oben in die zweite Ebene befördert. Das passiert, weil das Überqueren jeder Linie das Licht und die Ebenenhöhe verändern kann. So können sie Elemente im Spiel verändern und etwa Zahlen anzeigen.
