articles.title: Applebee's exposed customers' personal data after leaving database password in app | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Applebee’s has fixed a security flaw that allowed anyone to access the personal information of its registered customers, after a researcher found a password for an internal database inside Applebee’s mobile app, TechCrunch has learned.
The popular restaurant chain confirmed on Thursday that it had taken action to address the security issue to prevent any unauthorized access to its customer database.
TechCrunch withheld publication of this story until the bug was confirmed to be fixed.
Robert Wiggins, a U.K.-based cybersecurity researcher at What Security, discovered the security lapse earlier this month. Wiggins is no stranger to discovering security issues, including exposed or sensitive information that should not be publicly accessible.
For this latest discovery, Wiggins used AI to help find the credential buried inside thousands of lines of source code in Applebee’s Android app, which has more than a million downloads on Google Play. The credential allowed access to the company’s customer database.
Storing a password or private key in software, known as hardcoding credentials, is one of the most severe types of security vulnerabilities because anyone with the app can extract the key and use it to log in to a remote system as if they were an authorized user.
Wiggins said that the hardcoded credential could have also allowed a malicious attacker to modify customer data in the database.

articles.title: London, Ontario is Canada's number one city for partying: report
articles.summary:
According to a recent report by Uber, Ontario is home to Canada’s top partying destination, but it’s not Toronto that holds the honour.
Releasing its fifth annual Nightlife Index on Wednesday, Oct. 28, the ridesharing app revealed that, of all places, London, Ontario, is the number one city in the country for partying.
It makes sense, given the city’s substantial student population, but a city’s got to be really good at partying to dethrone one like Toronto, which boasts a population nearly 10 times the size.
This marks the fourth time the Ontario city has landed the first-place slot, after being dethroned just once by Toronto in 2024.
Toronto didn’t even manage to land in the top three Canadian cities for partying, as it turns out. Winnipeg secured a second-place finish, while Lethbridge, Alberta, came in third.
Toronto ended up in fifth place, sandwiched between Kitchener-Waterloo in fourth and Halifax in sixth. And as someone who has lived in both Halifax and Toronto, I’d argue that those two positions ought to be swapped.
Since the list was created using aggregated and anonymized data from Uber and Uber Eats, such as late-night trips and food orders, I guess I stand corrected.
The study also showed that New Year’s Eve, Halloween Night and Halloween Weekend are the three biggest holidays for partying (no surprise there), and that, on average, Canadians stay out the latest on Halloween.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.summary:
An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers’ machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident.
The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont. Both Beaumont and the CTO and co-founder of security firm Phorian said that version 2.1.313 was distributed through Anthropic’s official account on Cursor. So far, neither Cursor nor Anthropic has explained how the attackers gained control of the account.
In search of cloud credentials
“It was a supply-chain compromise where the attacker gained access to the official distribution channel,” Phorian CTO and co-founder Luke Roberts told Ars. “The malicious version 2.1.313 was posted to the official Anthropic account, effectively superseding 2.1.312. Extensions auto-update in Cursor by default, but users can configure this in settings.” Phorian has more details here.
Anthropic has yet to issue public notice of the incident to customers.

articles.title: Hackers vaciaron las billeteras de unos 700 usuarios de Polymarket y robaron al menos USD 2,7 millones
articles.summary:
Polymarket suspendió durante cerca de una hora las operaciones de su plataforma internacional el 29 de octubre, después de que hackers vaciaran las billeteras de cientos de usuarios. Según firmas de análisis de datos cripto, unos 710 usuarios perdieron al menos USD 2,7 millones. La empresa prometió reembolsar a todos los afectados.
Polymarket es una plataforma donde los usuarios apuestan sobre el resultado de eventos, desde las elecciones legislativas de Estados Unidos hasta la fecha de lanzamiento de un videojuego. La versión internacional funciona con criptomonedas y está prohibida en Estados Unidos y en otros países, según Wired.
La empresa informó que uno de sus proveedores externos fue vulnerado y que derivó el caso a las autoridades. “Cualquiera que haya sido afectado será compensado”, escribió en un comunicado citado por BleepingComputer. Polymarket pasó a un modo en el que solo se permitía cancelar órdenes a las 14:05, hora del Este de Estados Unidos.
Las operaciones volvieron a la normalidad a las 15:05, según el relato de la propia empresa recogido por BleepingComputer. Los primeros reclamos de billeteras vaciadas aparecieron cerca de las 13:30, de acuerdo con The Washington Post, y varios traderes conocidos se quejaron de pérdidas en la red social X.
El código malicioso venía de una herramienta de medición web

articles.title: Google Discloses PageBreak AI Security Agent That Found 500+ XSS Bugs
articles.summary:
According to a paper published by Google, its AI-powered security agent has uncovered more than 500 XSS vulnerabilities across its web applications since entering full operation in January. Google PageBreak uses Gemini models to autonomously investigate potential vulnerabilities, but reports them only after deterministic validators successfully reproduce the exploit against a running application, resulting in a near-zero false-positive rate.
With PageBreak, every vulnerability hypothesis is tested against a running environment with a real exploit, such as executing JavaScript for XSS, writing to a world-readable location for path traversal, or triggering outbound DNS for RCE. Michał Bentkowski, information security engineer at Google, explains:
Early on in the development of PageBreak, we made a conscious decision to prioritize deterministic validation. Rather than simply hypothesizing bugs based on code patterns, the system closes the loop by verifying potential flaws against running environments. This approach results in a near-zero false positive rate, ensuring that we avoid overloading product teams with unverified vulnerability reports.
Google also retains non-deterministic findings internally to seed deeper future scans, identify gaps in its validation capabilities, and guide the development of new validators. These unverified candidates are not sent to product teams, keeping their attention focused on high-confidence vulnerabilities. Bentkowski writes:

The Quiet Hours: Why Overnight Network Monitoring Matters
When most of us are asleep, the unseen guardians of the digital world are wide awake, watching over the networks and systems that power our businesses. These overnight hours, particularly around 3am, are critical for IT infrastructure because this is when unusual activity often surfaces, whether due to cyberattacks exploiting off-peak vulnerabilities or system failures that quietly escalate. Despite the stillness outside, the digital realm is vibrant with activity-some routine, some threatening, and all vital to understand.
Understanding what happens during these quiet hours can offer invaluable insights into maintaining robust, resilient networks. IT teams who specialize in overnight monitoring have unique perspectives on system behavior, risk mitigation, and proactive maintenance – lessons that any business relying on digital operations can benefit from. Their vigilance helps prevent small issues from snowballing into costly incidents, ensuring systems are ready to support daily operations when the workday begins.

articles.summary:
Chinese hackers build PHP2SHELL exploit, use it to root 25 servers, breach US government-affiliated firewalls
Palo Alto Networks firewalls running outdated OS seem to be the target
- Researchers report the first confirmed PHP2Shell compromises, targeting organizations linked to the US government
- Attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Linux privilege-escalation flaw to gain root access and persistence
- Breaches progressed from initial compromise to Active Directory attacks within minutes, underscoring patching urgency
We now have confirmation of the first successful exploits of the infamous PHP2Shell vulnerability discovered earlier this month.
The news comes courtesy of cybersecurity outfit Dream, who claim to have seen attackers breach organizations affiliated with the US government.
PHP2Shell is a name given to two critical-severity vulnerabilities found in PHP. When they were first disclosed, most of the cybersecurity community went full panic mode, given that PHP powers roughly 70% of all websites and web apps on the internet, and there was no patch at the time. The flaws allegedly enabled complete website takeover, and some government and education organizations in Europe even preemptively shut down their websites, in anticipation of mass exploitation attempts.

A primer on key AI LLM concepts — KV cache, weights, quantization, and how inference actually works
Everyone knows about hallucination, but a handful of topics are often unclear. We'll fix that.
As hardware for running local AI models continues to move to the forefront, such as Nvidia's RTX Spark, a new set of acronyms, definitions, and terminology is popping up. Given the pace of releases, we've put together a list of AI's new nomenclature to familiarize you with new concepts and pieces of terminology that you'll likely see in Tom's Hardware Premium articles.
This primer should get you started on the world of AI and be handy the next time news on the topic comes around, and possibly when you're downloading some models to try out and tweak for yourself. articles.summary:
Editor's take: Many research and enterprise organizations are trying to force staff to use AI tools wherever and whenever they can. Needless to say, the backlash is as strong as the C-suite's stubborn determination to push AI, even where there is absolutely no need for it.
David Durman might be the first employee to receive a special exemption from using AI tools on religious grounds. The 45-year-old research administrator at the University of Kentucky identifies as a humanist, a belief system that apparently requires him to avoid AI-based workflows. Depuis sa présentation en juillet, Cloud Rebuild a gagné plusieurs fonctions, dont une option d'effacement sécurisé des données et la possibilité pour les administrateurs informatiques de déclencher une réinstallation à distance. Une réinstallation complète, même lorsque Windows est inaccessible

L'opération se déroule dans l'environnement de récupération Windows (WinRE), accessible après plusieurs échecs de démarrage. Plus besoin de préparer une clé USB sur un autre PC ni de disposer d'une image de récupération locale. Vous pouvez également lancer la fonction lorsque Windows fonctionne encore, depuis les Paramètres > Système > Récupération.

articles.title: Critical Linux kernel flaw allows remote root attacks on MPTCP servers
articles.summary:
Security researchers at Anthropic have developed an exploit for a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute commands as root on servers running Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listeners.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, also affects ordinary TCP connections, although remote code execution has not been publicly demonstrated on servers without an MPTCP listener.
Multipath TCP (MPTCP) is a TCP feature that lets a single connection use multiple network paths at the same time to improve performance and reliability. It is commonly used in environments where devices have multiple network connections, such as Wi-Fi and cellular networks.
CVE-2026-98432 is a use-after-free vulnerability in the kernel's IPv4 TCP networking code that received a severity score of 9.8 out of 10 from the Linux kernel CVE team.
The vulnerability affects Linux kernels dating back to version 4.4, including widely used distributions such as Ubuntu, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), and Rocky Linux.
According to the Linux kernel advisory, the vulnerability stems from a race condition in how the kernel handles TCP connection requests, potentially causing a use-after-free condition.
"tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it," reads the advisory.

articles.title: « Le SMS de la mort » : ce simple message peut rendre votre smartphone inutilisable
articles.summary:
Le chercheur indépendant en cybersécurité Mark Blaszczyk a rendu publique une faille zero day sur Android. Pas de panique, elle a été corrigée par Google avant et votre téléphone ne court aucun risque. Mais le fonctionnement de cette faille est tout à fait intéressant.
Un « SMS of Death » qui peut faire des dégâts sur votre smartphone Android
Mark Blaszczyk a donc publié le résultat de ses recherches sur Internet et il décrit en détail comment fonctionne cette faille. Elle se trouve dans le composant Android plus très utilisé, un ancien format de « data SMS », utilisé historiquement pour des notifications de MMS ou des contenus push. Il n’apparaît jamais à l’écran, puisqu’il se contente de fonctionner en arrière-plan. Le problème vient en réalité d’une conversion mal encadrée : Android lit la longueur de l’en-tête d’un message comme un entier long, puis la convertit en entier signé 32 bits sans vérifier que la valeur reste plausible.
Avec la séquence de cinq octets 88 80 80 80 00, cette valeur devient -2147483648. Face à ça, Android tente alors de créer un tableau d’octets de cette taille négative, ce qui tue le processus com.android.phone qui gère… la téléphonie, rien que ça. Chaque message malformé comme cela coupe donc le service durant une à deux secondes, le temps que ce processus redémarre. Ce qui coupe tout simplement les appels en cours.
Une faille bien particulière, puisqu’elle est qualifiée de zero click, c’est-à-dire que la victime n’a rien à ouvrir, installer ou v…

articles.title: Google: Agentic AI Will Drive New Demands on Data Center CPUs - EE Times
articles.summary:
The requirements of agentic AI are placing new demands on data center CPUs and infrastructure as a whole, Mark Lohmeyer, vice president and general manager for AI and computing infrastructure at Google Cloud, told EE Times.
“Chat is relatively straightforward—there’s a question and an answer, and it relies heavily on inference across GPUs or TPUs,” he said. “With agents, the nature of those interactions is changing quite a bit.”
With agents, the user’s high-level intent can be broken down into subtasks and assigned to a team of agents that can access other APIs, visit websites, write and run code—CPU tasks. Sessions can be much longer and can involve multiple human users, which means context and state need to be preserved over potentially days or weeks.
“Agents are often bursty, and often idle,” he said. “They don’t do anything for [say] a day or two until you come back to them, or maybe until some API responds… It’s unique from older CPU workloads, in that it needs to be stateful over a long period of time, but is often idle during that period of time, and then when it’s not idle, it’s highly bursty.”
Handling this in a performant and secure way is a big challenge the industry is facing today, Lohmeyer said.
“Demand is already very high and is growing rapidly,” he said. “So, how do we provide the infrastructure that can support that growth and do it cost-effectively?”

articles.title: Anthropic expected to receive high 'junk' rating from credit agencies following IPO, FT report says | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Anthropic is expected to receive a high “junk” rating from credit rating agencies following its initial public offering, according to a report from the Financial Times.
The FT says the investment giant Blackstone, the anchor investor in a recent $63 billion deal to finance Anthropic’s chips, told investors in the deal that it expects the AI lab to receive a “high” junk rating after its IPO. Previously, the FT notes, Blackstone had said the opposite: that the Claude maker would receive an investment-grade rating (indicating low risk for lenders) before 2027 rolls around.
Now Blackstone expects double B range rating, the top tier of speculative “junk” grade, according to the reporting.
TechCrunch reached out to Anthropic and Blackstone but both declined to comment.
Blackstone’s forecast is just a prediction, but naturally, a high junk rating would make it more difficult and costlier for Anthropic to raise the money to keep funding its massive spending that has undergirded its business. The lab has been on a spending spree, racking up large compute power deals throughout the past 12 months, which has worried investors.
Anthropic officially filed to go public earlier this week, kicking off a wave of speculation about how the massive IPO would impact the broader AI industry.

articles.title: The AI hardware crunch has reached the humble circuit board
articles.summary:
Ripple effect: PC makers have spent most of this year chasing memory and graphics chips as AI data centers bought up whatever they could. Now the circuit boards those chips sit on are reportedly running short, too. The same factories are busy with far pricier boards for AI servers, so PC orders are getting pushed to the back of the line.
While planning their 2027 lineups, executives at HP and Dell have started worrying about whether they'll get enough boards, Nikkei Asia reports. Even with PC shipments possibly sliding again next year, one manager at an American PC maker said the company still can't get enough of them.
The trouble is that a high-end AI server board can stack dozens of layers of low-loss laminate and specialty glass fabric. So each one ties up far more material and factory time than a desktop motherboard ever would. Cloud giants are happy to pay up for them – Amazon even bought a roughly NT$1.59 billion stake in Taiwanese board maker Gold Circuit Electronics in September.
Every one of those boards starts as a sheet of copper-clad laminate. One Taiwanese PC maker told Nikkei that laminate now costs at least 12 times what it did in July. Meanwhile, one of the world's biggest laminate suppliers says its order book already stretches into 2030. That's despite plans to triple its capacity by 2028.
So board makers are quoting longer and longer waits. One told Nikkei that lead times on a good chunk of its products have doubled. Another said a fresh order placed today …

articles.summary:
For a genuine fright this Halloween, you can turn your gaze to the southern border, where ravenous, flesh-eating maggots are festering and have taken to eating people’s pets.
This week, the country’s New World Screwworm (NWS) infestation spread to a third state, Arizona, which joins New Mexico and Texas in being plagued by the horrifying parasites. To date, 74 animal cases have been identified in the US since the flies re-invaded the country in June.
The flies lay hundreds of eggs in wounds and moist orifices of animals, and the resulting voracious maggots feast on their victims. The maggots resemble screws and tortuously bore and twist into living flesh, causing severe, sometimes fatal wounds, before dropping to the ground to develop into adults.
Because of their ability to ravage livestock, the flies were eliminated from the country in the 1960s through aerial releases of sterile male flies, which thwart successful breeding. For years, they were held at bay using a biological barrier along the Darién Gap at the border of Panama and Colombia. But the barrier was breached in 2022, and the flies have made their way back to the US through Central America.
No one is safe
While they are largely seen as a threat to the livestock industry, they can also devastate wildlife, domestic pets, and in rarer cases, humans. articles.summary:
PsiQuantum turns its photonics know-how into an optical switch for supercharging AI data center GPU networks — 8x8 lab prototype loses less light than rivals, with plans to develop larger devices
Google’s mirror switches have 136 ports; PsiQuantum’s chip has eight, with larger devices in development.
PsiQuantum, a quantum computing company, announced in a release earlier this week that it has turned its low-loss silicon photonics into an optical switch for use in AI data centers. Every optical switch typically comes with loss of light: the more light a switch receives, the less reaches the other side, with the amount of light lost measured in decibels. Typical data center optics can tolerate half the light (3 dB) being lost. PsiQuantum's switch debuted with a demo that typically loses only 1.2 dB of signal, or about a quarter of the light in lab tests, and the all-optical switch can achieve it without an amplifier. The prototype is, however, comparatively small, with eight inputs and outputs (8x8) against competitors’ 32 to 300, but the company says larger devices are in development.
The optical circuit switch (OCS) passes light straight through, from fiber to fiber, without converting it to or from electrical signals. Regular data center switches make that conversion at every hop, which takes power and adds latency. An OCS, instead, uses a fixed light path that it maintains until a change is ordered. articles.title: Once again, NASA is asking for ideas to rescue Hubble from certain death

The Hubble Space Telescope still shines in the eyes of astronomers after 36 years in orbit, but it is not as nimble as it once was. Left alone, the observatory will plunge back into the atmosphere in the early-to-mid-2030s, closing the book on one of the most famous scientific instruments of the century.
NASA last raised the orbit of Hubble in 2002, when the Space Shuttle Columbia visited the observatory for a servicing mission. The final shuttle servicing flight in 2009 did not reboost the telescope’s orbit, and with the retirement of the shuttle fleet two years later, Hubble has steadily lost altitude with no way to stave off eventual destruction.
The space agency released a Request For Information (RFI) on Thursday asking commercial companies for ideas on how to reboost, service, or a controlled disposal of Hubble. Responses are due November 30. Specifically, NASA is looking for information about companies’ current and near-term capabilities for capturing Hubble and boosting it to an altitude of at least 373 miles (600 km), enhancing the telescope’s performance, or guiding Hubble to a controlled reentry.
“The requirement includes that the boost and/or servicing mission must not harm the HST and that this mission is expected to occur by 2032,” NASA wrote in the RFI. The contractor would be responsible for providing the launch vehicle, servicing spacecraft, mission operations, and “crew if applicable.”

Projetos de código aberto permitem rodar títulos exclusivos em outras plataformas, mas exigem uma cópia original dos games.
Uma semana após o primeiro jailbreak do Nintendo Switch 2 via software, diversos jogos exclusivos da Nintendo já rodam em outras plataformas. Publicações no X/Twitter mostram títulos do console funcionando em PCs, no iPhone 18 Pro e até em um computador com macOS.
Ferramentas de código aberto têm facilitado o processo, como o software ns2jb, disponibilizado em 22 de outubro. Jogos como Mario Kart World, Dragon Age e Zelda foram disponibilizados em ports no GitHub sob a licença MIT, que permite o acesso ao código para pesquisa e testes. São projetos que não incluem os jogos em si: para executá-los, é necessário ter uma cópia original de cada título.
Por isso, a disponibilização dos ports, por si só, não configura pirataria. A infração ocorre quando há distribuição ou download não autorizado das imagens ISO dos títulos.
A Nintendo, porém, tem um histórico de ações contra emuladores e ferramentas de acesso a seus jogos. Em 2024, a empresa conseguiu derrubar o Yuzu, conhecido emulador de Nintendo Switch, e pediu a remoção de outras ferramentas semelhantes hospedadas no GitHub.
Mais recentemente, um usuário do Reddit foi condenado a pagar US$ 4,5 milhões (pouco mais de R$ 24 milhões) por violações envolvendo mais de 30 jogos exclusivos do Switch.

Two different sleep trackers can read the same night and print two different deep-sleep percentages, and the internet’s reference numbers argue among themselves the same way, with figures from 10 to 25 percent all claiming to be the norm. How much deep sleep you need comes down to one benchmark: healthy adults spend about 13 to 23 percent of total sleep in deep sleep. The disagreement has a structure, and it takes about five minutes to learn. What follows is the benchmark, why wrist readings of sleep stages wobble, and a five-question check to run before paying for any tracker.
How Much Deep Sleep Do Adults Need? Two Bands Behind the Conflicting Percentages
Two citation bands explain most of the conflict in deep-sleep numbers. Under the AASM staging framework, healthy adults spend about 13 to 23 percent of total sleep in the N3 stage, while 10 to 20 percent is the looser band many sources still quote. A quoted 25 percent usually means retelling inflated the range.
The fix is a two-second reading habit, check the band’s origin before the percentage. AASM staging figures put N3 at 13 to 23 percent of total sleep, commonly cited figures answer with the looser 10 to 20 percent band, and the number 25 percent is what inflated retelling looks like. Results on the high end usually come from sources quoting the wider bands, so the argument never ends until the reader checks which one is in use.

articles.title: Salesforce’s M&A spree continues with a reported $375M deal for defense tech startup Rune | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Salesforce has agreed to acquire Rune Technologies, a startup that builds AI software to help the U.S. military predict supply needs and manage logistics from the field, for $375 million in cash and stock, Resilience Media reported.
The acquisition underscores Salesforce’s push into defense tech through Missionforce, its business unit serving national security and defense agencies. Since Missionforce launched last year, its business has grown 80% year over year, driven in part by a new 10-year, $5.6 billion contract with the U.S. Army, the company said in a blog post. By integrating Rune’s frontline logistics data, Missionforce will extend beyond back-office administrative planning to support battlefield operations.
Since its founding in 2024, Rune has raised a total of $30 million from investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Point72 Ventures, and IQT, a CIA-backed nonprofit venture firm formerly known as In-Q-Tel. The startup was last valued at $127 million when it raised a Series A led by Human Capital last year, according to PitchBook.
Salesforce has been on an acquisition spree this year. In addition to Rune, the CRM giant agreed to buy AI agent platform Fin (formerly Intercom) for $3.6 billion, bought Qualified for $1.2 billion, and signed an agreement to buy Listen Labs after the startup walked away from a $125 million Series C term sheet at a $1.5 billion valuation, as TechCrunch reported.
Salesforce didn’t respond to a request for comment.

IPVanish finally launches a dedicated IP — and it fixes one of the VPN's biggest gaps
The new feature gives IPVanish users a static IP address that belongs to them alone
- IPVanish has launched a dedicated IP, a feature reviewers have long flagged as missing.
- It gives you a fixed VPN IP address that no other user shares, with five locations at launch.
- It's aimed at people who need reliable logins and remote access, but there's a privacy trade-off to weigh up.
IPVanish has launched a dedicated IP, an optional add-on that fills one of the most noticeable gaps in its feature list.
Until now, the provider only offered shared, dynamic IP addresses. Reviewers have repeatedly pointed to the missing option as a weak spot, particularly for remote workers and small businesses, and as recently as last week, rivals were still listing it as something IPVanish couldn't do.
NordVPN and Surfshark have offered dedicated IPs for years, so the launch brings IPVanish closer in line with the best VPN services on the market.
How IPVanish's dedicated IP works
When you connect to a VPN normally, you share an IP address with everyone else on that server, and you might get a different one each session. A dedicated IP flips that: it's a unique address assigned to a single user, and it stays the same every time you connect.

Modern IT infrastructure is a lot like building blocks. Some of it sits in the cloud, some in European server colocation facilities, and some runs on a company’s own hardware. articles.title: Un agujero negro que se parte en dos suena imposible. Un nuevo estudio dice que la física deja una rendija abierta
articles.summary:
La física de los agujeros negros está rodeada aún de muchas preguntas sin resolver. Por ejemplo, sabemos que dos agujeros negros pueden fusionarse para dar lugar a uno más grande, ¿pero puede un gran agujero negro dividirse en dos más pequeños? Tradicionalmente se ha pensado que no, pues iría en contra de las leyes de la física. Sin embargo, un equipo de científicos de la Universidad Federico II de Nápoles, la Sorbona de París y la Universidad del Sur de Dinamarca acaba de encontrar un atajo teórico por el que sí sería posible.
Una cuestión de orden. Según la segunda ley de la termodinámica, la entropía de un sistema aislado siempre tiende a aumentar. A muy grandes rasgos, la entropía hace referencia al desorden, o la cantidad de conformaciones microscópicas distintas que puede alcanzar dicho sistema. Por eso, siempre se dice que el Universo tiende al desorden.
Generalmente, en la mayoría de objetos, la entropía es proporcional a la cantidad de materia, por lo que si se rompe en dos un pedazo de papel su entropía no disminuirá, ya que la suma de los dos pedazos sigue siendo la misma. Con los agujeros negros, la cosa cambia, ya que en ellos la entropía es proporcional al área del horizonte de sucesos, que crece con el cuadrado de la masa irreducible del agujero negro. Si un agujero negro se divide en dos, el área de sus horizontes de sucesos será más pequeña, de modo que la entropía disminuye. Iría contra las leyes de la física.
La clave está en el giro. Según los autores de e…

articles.title: Doom n’a jamais tourné comme ça : un Raspberry Pi, deux IA et aucun moteur de jeu
articles.summary:
Après les calculatrices, les imprimantes et même les tests de grossesse, Doom continue de s'inviter un peu partout. Cette fois, un développeur a fait fonctionner une version simplifiée du célèbre FPS sur un Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W. Sa particularité ? Le jeu n'est pas exécuté par un moteur classique, mais recréé image après image par une intelligence artificielle.
Faire tourner Doom sur à peu près n'importe quoi est devenu une tradition chez les bidouilleurs. En 2020, Foone Turing avait même réussi à le rendre jouable sur un test de grossesse numérique, après en avoir remplacé l'écran et le processeur.
Avec son projet Tinyworldformer, le développeur SheepSeb pousse l'expérience dans une autre direction. Plutôt que d'adapter le code d'un jeu à une machine peu puissante, il a entraîné une IA à reproduire son fonctionnement. Le tout sur un Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W, une carte à quelques euros équipée d'une puce RP2350, de deux cœurs pouvant atteindre 150 MHz et de seulement 520 Ko de mémoire vive. Doom avait déjà été porté sur un Raspberry Pi Pico en 2022, mais cette fois, l'expérience ne repose plus sur l'exécution du jeu original.
Un Doom lite sans moteur de jeu, mais avec deux IA
Tinyworldformer repose sur deux petits réseaux neuronaux. Le premier est un world model, ou modèle de monde : entraîné à partir de parties enregistrées, il reçoit une image et une action du joueur, puis prédit l'image suivante. Il ne calcule donc pas les conséquences des actions à partir des règles original…

articles.title: Why Banks Need Thousands of Test Cycles Before AI Agents Spend Money - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
A bank can forgive a chatbot that gives a clumsy answer. It cannot forgive an agent that pays the same invoice twice. As software begins to act on behalf of customers, moving funds and settling bills without a person approving each step, the testing bar rises sharply.
That is why risk teams talk in thousands of test cycles, not dozens. Each cycle replays a payment scenario with small changes, and the goal is to see how the agent behaves when conditions drift. Teams that want a practical picture of how payment infrastructure is assembled and exercised can look at how FinteqHub explains the connections between financial services and technology providers.
What Changes When Software Holds the Wallet
A traditional payment flow has a human checkpoint. Someone clicks, confirms a code, or signs off a batch. An AI agent removes that checkpoint by design, because the whole point is speed and autonomy. Removing the human does not remove the need for judgment. It moves the judgment into rules, limits and monitoring, and every one of those has to be proven before launch.
Why one successful run proves very little
An agent that pays a utility bill correctly on Monday has shown it can handle Monday. Language models are probabilistic, so the same prompt can produce slightly different actions on different runs. Risk officers would rather see forty identical passes than one flawless demo.

The limited partners who provide the capital to venture firms — the “money behind the money” — are feeling great right now. They’re in uncharted territory in many ways, but also potentially exceedingly lucrative territory.
Normally, LPs typically spread their bets across many firms to diversify their own portfolios. They write checks to emerging managers and established ones, to generalist firms and specialists. The goal is a strong return, but also to minimize risk.
That’s the typical playbook. But typical is out the window. OpenAI and Anthropic’s valuations have shot up so quickly that nearly everyone has piled into the same two companies on the way up, often inside the same venture firm, despite the longstanding venture convention of avoiding investments that conflict with one another. No one is complaining, either. The LPs I speak with seem unbothered by this big gamble, given the potential returns; they’re expecting a bonanza.
But they do see danger ahead, even if they describe this as a “yellow light” situation, and they’re uneasy about how quickly VCs are coming back to raise new funds.
I talked about all of it recently with Beezer Clarkson of LGT Capital Partners, a Zurich-based diversified asset manager, and Amit Bhatti of TrueBridge, a Chapel Hill firm that focuses solely on venture. This conversation has been edited for length.

articles.title: Qué es la dirección IP, cómo encontrarla y por qué es importante para navegar por internet
articles.summary:
Cada vez que una persona ingresa a una página web, utiliza una aplicación o conecta su celular a una red Wi-Fi, su dispositivo necesita identificarse para intercambiar información. En ese proceso interviene la dirección IP, un número que permite reconocer a los equipos dentro de una red y hacer posible la comunicación a través de internet.
Aunque suele pasar desapercibida, esta identificación digital cumple una función fundamental en la navegación cotidiana. También puede resultar útil cuando una conexión presenta fallas, se necesita configurar una impresora o cámara de seguridad, o se quiere comprobar si una red privada virtual (VPN) está ocultando la dirección habitual.
Conocer la dirección IP no requiere instalar programas ni tener conocimientos avanzados de informática. Existen herramientas gratuitas en internet que permiten consultar la dirección pública, mientras que la dirección privada puede encontrarse directamente desde la configuración de una computadora o un teléfono.
¿Qué es una dirección IP y para qué sirve?
La dirección IP, sigla de Internet Protocol (protocolo de internet), es una identificación numérica asignada a un dispositivo cuando se conecta a una red. Su función consiste en permitir que los equipos envíen y reciban información, de manera que los datos puedan llegar al destino correcto.

WavKong today announced the commercial launch of its V2700 long-range Wi-Fi 6 router following the successful fulfillment of all Kickstarter orders. Its approach to whole-home Wi-Fi is built on a simple principle: Improve the wireless signal at its source, then use the fewest nodes necessary to deliver reliable coverage across even the largest or most complex homes.
From the upstairs bedroom where a daughter streams and studies, to a garage, a backyard gathering, or a security camera on a barn, reliable Wi-Fi should reach the places people actually use—not just the room closest to the router.Developed over six years, WavKong's proprietary RPU (Radio Processing Unit) chip brings base-station-grade digital signal processing to home Wi-Fi. In company testing at a single-story, wood-frame residence in California, one V2700 provided up to 15,000 square feet of combined indoor-outdoor Wi-Fi coverage. articles.title: The hidden threat in Anthropic’s prospectus: diseconomies of scale - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
The hidden threat in Anthropic’s prospectus: diseconomies of scale
As potentially the largest IPO in history, Anthropic PBC is breaking new ground. Its prospectus lists 88 risk factors covering 93 pages alone. From artificial intelligence posing an existential threat to humanity to the possibility AI will blackmail people, the company lists a litany of risks that should make any potential Anthropic investor wary.
One potentially company-sinking risk factor, however, does not explicitly appear in the prospectus: diseconomies of scale.
Diseconomies of scale occur when a company’s average cost of producing each unit of output increases as the company grows.
You would think that given the time and effort that Anthropic devoted to ensuring its list of risk factors was complete that they would have included this one. There is a reason, however, that they missed it, despite the fact that diseconomies of scale is the elephant in the room.
We’ve been down this road before with cloud computing. The fundamental economic driver of the hyperscaler clouds was economies of scale: the larger they became, the lower their cost of each unit of output, leading to massive growth and profitability over time.
Since the AI boom requires massive data center buildouts just as cloud computing does, it might be reasonable to assume that AI will experience the same economic benefits of massive growth that cloud computing enjoyed.

En países como Colombia, el 25% de las pymes registró incidentes de phishing, el 20% enfrentó ataques vinculados con vulnerabilidades de software y el 15% tuvo problemas asociados con accesos remotos externos.
A los anteriores riesgos se suman uno menos conocido: las aplicaciones falsas de inteligencia artificial (IA), que buscan instalar programas maliciosos bajo la apariencia de servicios conocidos.
Por qué las empresas pequeñas son un objetivo para los ciberdelincuentes
Carolina Mojica, gerente de Productos para el Consumidor para NOLA y SOLA en Kaspersky, afirmó que existe una percepción equivocada entre algunos empresarios: “Creen que no van a tener ciberataques porque son pequeñas y que no son un blanco, y por el contrario sí lo son”.
El tamaño de un negocio no reduce el interés de los ciberdelincuentes. Las pymes suelen manejar datos de clientes, transacciones, contactos de proveedores y archivos operativos que pueden ser utilizados para extorsión, fraude o venta ilegal.

La crise des composants mémoire et la hausse des prix continuent d'impacter durement les divers appareils informatiques grand public. Smartphones, tablettes, PC… Tout a augmenté, même les consoles ! Cette crise, pas près de se terminer, pourrait toutefois trouver une issue grâce à une nouvelle technologie baptisée Z2RAM.
Développée par Nagare Labs, une entreprise cofondée par les professeurs Suman Datta et Shimeng Yu du Georgia Institute of Technology, elle bénéficie d'un financement de 5 millions de dollars mené par Playground Global, dont Pat Gelsinger, ancien PDG d'Intel, est un associé.
Une architecture combinant trois technologies de mémoire
La Z2RAM ambitionne de réunir la rapidité de la SRAM, la densité de la DRAM et les possibilités d'empilement vertical de la NAND, avec une consommation énergétique réduite et une fabrication nettement simplifiée.
La SRAM, utilisée dans les caches des processeurs, est rapide mais occupe beaucoup de place. La DRAM, utilisée dans les si chères barrettes de RAM, offre une densité supérieure, mais une vitesse moindre. Quant à la NAND des SSD, elle privilégie la densité grâce à son empilement vertical, au détriment des performances.

articles.title: AI semiconductor industry trends: from chips to systems - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
6 insights from the GSA Women’s Leadership Initiative: AI semiconductor industry trends turn the chip race into a systems race
For decades, the semiconductor industry competed on one thing: the individual chip. One of the biggest AI semiconductor industry trends now under way is the shift toward treating chips as components of much larger systems. Performance, cost and reliability are now determined across the package, the rack and the supply chain, not inside a single die.
That shift moves the hardest problems upstream. Packaging, connectivity, yield, sourcing and verification used to come after design, but now they shape it from the first day. AI is shortening development cycles at the same time as it adds to the complexity engineers have to manage. The next phase will be defined by how well companies coordinate across that whole system.
“I think the AI system is our new chips,” said Letizia Giuliano, vice president of product management and marketing at Qualcomm Technologies Inc. “If we were optimizing everything for the silicon in the past, now these days we’re optimizing everything for the system.”
Giuliano and other industry experts spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and co-host Alison Kosik at the GSA Women’s Leadership Initiative event in Palo Alto, California. The interviews covered AI semiconductor industry trends, optical interconnects, advanced packaging, AI-driven yield learning, physical AI, strategic sourcing and AI-assisted chip design.

articles.title: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison thinks AI could make us all rich through a universal high income – but governments will need to change
articles.summary:
Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison thinks AI could make us all rich through a universal high income – but governments will need to change
Ellison says AI will make the world "healthier and wealthier"
Speaking on-stage at the company's recent AI World conference, Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison declared AI could eventually make everyone "healthier and wealthier".
Apparently unfazed by the technology's impacts on humanity, Ellison does acknowledge that governments need to have a shift in mindset to adapt to this new future.
In a Q&A during the conference's hotly anticipated final keynote, Ellison outlined a future where AI systems and robots could dramatically reduce the cost of goods and services. But rather than accepting the suggestion that AI would end up replacing us all, he argued that the technology would ultimately serve to make us more productive, allowing workers to achieve things that simply weren't possible before.
AI won't replace us, but it will change the economics of work in a lasting way

Hackers steal $6.3B from Binance in biggest-ever crypto heist
Hackers have stolen about $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from Binance, a major cryptocurrency exchange operator.
The heist is more than four times bigger than the previous largest crypto theft. TRM Labs Inc., a venture-backed blockchain intelligence startup, believes that both cyberattacks were carried out by a North Korean state-backed hacking group tracked as TraderTraitor.
About 40% of the stolen sum comprised stablecoins issued by three major crypto companies: Circle Internet Group Inc., Ripple Labs Inc. and Tether Ltd. They managed to freeze most of the funds before the hackers moved them out of reach. Binance, for its part, has set aside over $6.34 billion to cover users’ losses.
The hackers stole the funds by compromising several of the company’s wallets. One of them powers the infrastructure that Binance uses to process customers’ Ethereum transactions. According to TRM, the hackers breached the wallet late Thursday and sent its entire balance to a wallet they controlled.
TraderTraitor compromised Binance’s wallet by exploiting an Ethereum feature called EIP-7702 that the blockchain’s maintainers released last year. It enables a snippet of code called a smart contract to temporarily control a wallet. EIP-7702 only activates smart contracts if they receive authorization to run from the wallet’s operator. Como cancelar o Kindle+ (antigo Kindle Unlimited)
Assinatura do Kindle Unlimited, agora chamado de Kindle+, pode ser cancelada pelo celular ou computador em poucos passos
Se você deseja cancelar o Kindle Unlimited ou Kindle+, precisará usar o navegador do celular ou do PC para acessar a página de gerenciamento do serviço da Amazon. Se você cansou, precisa parar de pagar ou não vê mais utilidade no Kindle+, siga os passos abaixo para interromper as futuras cobranças mensais da assinatura.

articles.title: Google, Anthropic and others to support new AI crawling opt-out standard - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Google, Anthropic and others to support new AI crawling opt-out standard
Google LLC, Microsoft Corp., Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC today announced plans to support an upcoming website crawling standard.
The technology will enable website operators to block artificial intelligence developers from using their content to train their models.
Many websites contain a text file titled “robots.txt” that informs crawlers what content they may access. A publisher can use the file to block scraping across the board or only make specific webpages inaccessible. It’s also possible to include certain other instructions. For example, a company can ask crawlers not to visit its website too often.
Website operators historically used robots.txt files to manage how search engines interact with their properties. Nowadays, the technology also helps regulate the activity of the scrapers with which AI providers collect training data.
A company that wishes to disallow training-related scraping must make multiple edits to its website’s robots.txt file. In particular, it needs to add a separate entry for every single AI provider. If an AI provider uses multiple scrapers to collect data, each scraper requires its own robots.txt entry.
The crawling standard Google, Microsoft, Anthropic and OpenAI are backing aims to simplify the process. It would allow website operators to block all scrapers that collect training data for generative AI models with a single robots.txt entry. The setting wouldn’t app…

If the power goes out and your water supply is cut, how will you make your morning coffee? Put down that jar of instant granules — basic services might have failed, but your tastebuds haven't.
Drip coffee is an easy way to perk yourself up and boost your morale in a crisis (just pick up a ChemEx brewer or a simple dripper with some filter papers), but if you're aiming to conserve water then a shot of espresso is a better way to get your caffeine fix, so here I've focused on brewers for preparing shorter drinks.
Consider how you're going to store your emergency coffee supply, too. Whole beans will hold their flavor better than ground, and I recommend keeping them in an opaque, airtight container in a cool place (light, heat, air, and moisture are the enemies of aroma compounds). You'll need a grinder, too — look for one with burrs rather than blades so your coffee isn't chopped up in rough pieces.
If all that sounds like too much hassle in a crisis, opt for foil-sealed coffee pods instead. Both the Nanopresso and Dreame Ecceluxe Go below have adapters for brewing with single-serve capsules.

El fenómeno tiene nombre propio: ansiedad por IA. Según informó el Washington Post, los especialistas en salud mental advierten que llegó para quedarse. Los miedos van desde perder el trabajo hasta no poder distinguir lo real de lo fabricado por una máquina, y los terapeutas ya tienen respuestas concretas para quienes lo padecen.
La psiquiatra Tracy Foose, terapeuta en el Área de la Bahía de San Francisco, lo vivió en carne propia. Cuando empezó a publicar videos en redes sociales, algunos seguidores insistían en que era una influencer generada por computadora, algo que al principio le resultó halagador.
La sensación cambió cuando se puso a investigar. Descubrió que existen múltiples compañías que ofrecen crear dobles digitales capaces de replicar la voz y el rostro de cualquier persona.
“Me di cuenta de que alguien podría hacer un video que se apropiara tan completamente de mi imagen, mi voz, mi cara, que incluso yo podría creer que soy yo”, le dijo al Washington Post. El halago se transformó, según sus propias palabras, en “una forma de terror existencial”.

Fujifilm has revealed plans to increase its magnetic tape production capacity fivefold by fiscal 2028 in response to rising data storage demands driven by AI.
The Japanese company has allocated ¥10 billion ($63.3 million) to expand its Odawara plant near Tokyo, marking its largest investment in tape production for approximately 20 years.

Magnetic tape remains commercially useful because organisations can store enormous quantities of information without keeping the medium continuously connected to computer networks.

articles.title: Drones con tecnología láser descubren refugios aborígenes milenarios ocultos en los bosques de Australia
articles.summary:
La protección de testimonios culturales milenarios enfrenta la barrera de la geografía agreste. En vastas regiones del planeta, valiosos sitios arqueológicos permanecen ocultos bajo densos mantos vegetales y precipicios inaccesibles para las búsquedas a pie. Frente a este desafío en Australia, un equipo científico logró identificar tres refugios aborígenes desconocidos mediante drones con tecnología láser en las Montañas Azules.
Este hallazgo marca un avance significativo para la preservación patrimonial, al comprobar que herramientas aéreas avanzadas pueden documentar enclaves históricos resguardados durante milenios por el aislamiento geográfico. Hasta el momento, rastrear estos abrigos rocosos, cavidades naturales en paredes de piedra que funcionaron como resguardo y espacios ceremoniales para las comunidades originarias, dependía de extenuantes caminatas de inspección terrestre.
La topografía accidentada y la densa vegetación de la cordillera impidieron durante décadas un registro sistemático. Aunque el área reúne más de doscientos refugios catalogados con vestigios de ocupación humana, los especialistas calculan que apenas el diez por ciento del territorio ha sido relevado a fondo. Esta limitación mantenía la incógnita sobre la cantidad real de yacimientos y su estado ante factores como la erosión, los incendios y el avance urbano.

articles.title: Syrian Hacker Behind Fake Tweet That Triggered $136 Billion Market Drop Gets 42 Months in Prison
articles.summary:
Ahmad Umar Agha, a Syrian Electronic Army hacker known online as "Th3Pr0," has been sentenced by a U.S. federal court to 42 months in prison for his role in a hacking conspiracy that targeted Western news outlets.
The conspiracy was organized and led by members of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's inner circle, including the commander of Syria's General Intelligence Directorate, the U.S. Justice Department said on October 29.
The pro-Assad Syrian Electronic Army began its attacks in 2011. Its members sent phishing emails to steal employees' passwords, then used those passwords to deface websites, redirect web traffic, and hijack social media accounts, according to a 2014 FBI affidavit.
On April 23, 2013, the group hijacked the Associated Press's Twitter account and posted a false report that President Barack Obama had been injured in two explosions at the White House.
Twitter's message confirming a password reset for that account was sent to a Gmail account used primarily by Agha, the affidavit says.
The Justice Department said Agha carried out that hack, which caused a temporary $136 billion drop in the value of stocks in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. Agha later told Business Insider that a big drop in the Dow "was our goal of that hack attack" and that "it was a big victory for us."
Agha was first charged in June 2014 in a complaint that remained secret until March 2016. That month, the FBI added him and co-defendant Firas Dardar to its Cyber's Most Wanted list …

articles.title: Why Urgent Security Fixes Aren't Fixed. Observe, Prove, Act, Confirm Gets Them Moving
articles.summary:
The alert is critical. The fix is known. And the ticket sits in a queue for days. Security teams understand the risk, but the people who keep applications available need proof that the change won’t break anything.
Their concerns are practical. An IPS protection could block legitimate traffic. A configuration change could interrupt a service. An endpoint policy could affect an application the business depends on. Without evidence, the recommendation waits.
Safe remediation answers that hesitation with evidence. It tests the proposed action against your environment, applies the approved change, and confirms the result. Security and operations teams decide together, with facts.
The Cost of Leaving Protection in Detect
Many organizations already own protection they don’t enforce. Signatures sit inactive or in Detect mode while teams weigh false positives, inspection capacity, and business continuity. Meanwhile, applications and traffic patterns change, exceptions pile up, and policies drift away from how the environment runs today.
In the Safe Remediation white paper, 47% of the organizations measured had less than 50% protection enablement. Much of the capability they need is already in their environments.
Turning everything on isn’t the answer. Every activation carries risk. Teams need to know which changes matter for a given exposure, and how each will behave in production today.

Trezor has the customer's photos and description and has interviewed him on a video call. It is arranging for the wallet to be sent to its lab.
Trezor finds the report believable enough to warn buyers now. "Waiting for lab confirmation would leave CryptoBilis buyers exposed in the meantime," the company said.
No CryptoBilis buyer has reported losing funds to Trezor, which cannot see what customers hold in their wallets. The customer had moved his funds off the wallet before he found the board.

articles.title: Sam Altman defends OpenAI’s science blitz — CEO refuses to slow research as academics describe the influx as a 'giant bomb'
articles.summary:
Sam Altman says OpenAI won't slow science paper blitz — even though academics are calling it a 'giant bomb'
"It’s really cool and terrible at the same time", say researchers
- OpenAI will keep pushing AI’s scientific discoveries, Sam Altman says
- Some researchers are excited by the ‘fantastic’ breakthroughs
- But others warn that the pace of change is ‘psychologically taxing’
One of the promises that huge AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have made is that their machine learning models will help to solve some of the oldest problems in math and science. The pace of their discoveries has left many experts struggling to keep up, but OpenAI’s Sam Altman just has just said there’s much more in store — and not everyone is happy about that.
Speaking on the Cheeky Pint podcast, Altman outlined his belief that “Humanity deserves fundamental knowledge, and we should not be sitting on a major fundamental science discovery.”

"This is due to predictable, web-accessible staging paths used during full-package core upgrades," Wordfence said. "This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server during the upgrade window."

articles.summary:
TeamViewer has fixed a flaw that lets the machine being controlled in a remote session attack the computer that connected to control it. In a TeamViewer session, the computer that connects and takes control is the viewer, and the machine it controls is the host.
A malicious or compromised host can exploit the flaw to crash the viewer's TeamViewer and, depending on the platform, may also run code on the viewer's computer. This works only after the user starts a remote-control session to that host. The fix is in TeamViewer version 15.83.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-111585 and scored 8.8 out of 10, in the high range. It affects the TeamViewer Full Client on Windows, Linux, and macOS, the Windows Portable edition, and the Android Remote Control app, in all versions before 15.83.
For this flaw, TeamViewer's bulletin lists the Full Client, Portable, and Android app, but not the Host. The same 15.83 update fixes two other flaws in that bulletin that do affect the Host, so people running the Host should update as well.
Omri Dar, a researcher at security firm Remedio, published a technical account of the flaw on October 29. In this bug, he wrote, "the attacker is the host and the victim is the viewer."
In a remote session, the host tells the viewer how large its screen image is. The viewer uses that size to set aside memory, but the calculation can overflow and reserve too little. Screen data that arrives afterward is then written past the end of that space.

The web infrastructure and security company said it autonomously mitigated 18.2 million network-layer (L3) DDoS attacks and 14.4 trillion HTTP DDoS requests in the third quarter of 2026. That amounts to 197,400 attacks per day, or one attack every 0.44 seconds.
In comparison, a total of 13.2 million and 10.0 million L3 DDoS attacks were recorded in Q2 and Q1 2026, respectively. The increase has been linked to DDoS-for-hire booter or stresser services that are responsible for hundreds of thousands of attacks.
"Short-burst, low-bandwidth attacks lasting under 10 minutes and 1 Gbps surged by 208%," the Cloudforce One threat intelligence team said in its quarterly DDoS Threat Report shared with The Hacker News.
An interesting trend is the decline of hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps by 69% from the previous quarter – going from 805 attacks in Q2 to 251 in Q3 – likely as a result of law enforcement actions against AISURU, KimWolf, JackSkid, and Mossad earlier this March.
Still, the threat remains far from completely neutralized, given the emergence of new variants like Dysphoria and Evooo1Bot, Cloudflare warned.

articles.title: A Shared ChatGPT Link Could Run Attacker Code in Your Session and Read Private Chats
articles.summary:
A malicious ChatGPT share link could run an attacker's code in the logged-in session of anyone who opened it, allowing them to read their private conversations, researchers at the security firm Parameter showed.
The researchers reported the flaw through OpenAI's bug bounty program on October 18, and OpenAI fixed it eight days later and rated it P1, its most serious category.
The trap was an ordinary ChatGPT conversation shared via its public link. It could be sent the same way as any real shared chat: by email, as a chat message, as a support ticket, or as a social post.
The victim did not have to install anything, join a workspace, or sign in through the attacker. In the most reliable version of the attack, they opened the link and clicked ChatGPT's Preview button once. In a later version, Parameter set the page to open Preview on its own, so opening the link was the only step.
What the Attacker Could Do
Once the link opened, the attacker's code ran inside the victim's signed-in session with the same access as the real ChatGPT site. It listed the victim's recent conversations, opened a private chat that had never been shared with the attacker, and sent a small portion of it to a server controlled by the researchers.

Su instalación exige la descarga de archivos APK desde foros web de terceros y la desactivación manual de protocolos de seguridad nativos (como Google Play Protect). Al ejecutar estos instaladores para visualizar una película, el usuario introduce troyanos y software espía que operan de forma invisible en segundo plano.

articles.title: AI vendors are relearning the oldest rule in the data business
articles.summary:
AI vendors are relearning the oldest rule in the data business
Your data could soon be sharpening your competitors' tools
Long before anyone trained a model on customer data, the marketing data business worked out the terms for pooling it. Catalog retailers in the 1990s joined data cooperatives that combined their transaction histories so each member could find new buyers, and the arrangements held together because the rules were blunt.
A retailer contributed data to receive modeled prospects; no member got a rival's customer file; and a company that stopped contributing stopped receiving. Card fraud consortia run on similar give-to-get terms. Nobody would call these systems elegant, but every participant understood the trade.
Software vendors building AI features are now running into the same question, usually without the rules. Traditional software sat on top of a customer's data and operated on it. AI products learn from data, and on a multi-tenant platform, that learning rarely stays within a single account.
One company's records can sharpen the enrichment, lead scoring, and recommendations delivered to thousands of others. A vendor can improve its product for every customer by relying on the work of a few, and most contracts say nothing about whether that trade is fair. The customer still owns its data in any legal sense.
Ownership alone doesn't answer who benefits.
